0. What this document is, and what it is not

0. What this document is, and what it is not

Derived, not authored. Every table, card and diagram in this file is generated by docs/artifacts/tools/render_e2e_html.py from the canonical corpus JSON under docs/artifacts/. No statement, figure, count or edge in this document was written by hand, and nothing here is an independent source of truth. Where the corpus holds no value for something the engineering process expects, this document says not specified in corpus and records a named gap in section 12 rather than supplying a plausible substitute.

Status of the whole corpus

Distinct human_approval_status across every record shownpending

Distinct production_authorized across every record shownfalse

Distinct profile valuesas_is, synthetic_reference

Records in the artifact index321

Links in both link registries585

Every record in this document is printed with its own profile, origin, human_approval_status and production_authorized value on a guard line directly beneath its title, and the same four values are repeated in the data-guard attribute of that line. The census that produces those two rows is recomputed at render time from the records themselves; it is not a fixed statement about the corpus.

What this document does not assert

  • It makes no ISO 26262 conformity claim. Structural mapping of a record to a clause reference is not conformity, and the corpus states that distinction on its own coverage records.
  • It states no ASIL capability level for any product, process or organisation. ASIL values appear only as fields recorded inside individual corpus records, attributed to the record that carries them.
  • It records no Automotive SPICE assessment and no process capability rating.
  • It asserts no human approval and no review sign-off. Every record in the corpus carries human_approval_status: pending; an automated review is not an organisational or human confirmation measure.
  • It is not authorised for production use. Every record carries production_authorized: false.

The two profiles. as_is is a reconstruction of what the pinned foxBMS 2 sources demonstrate. synthetic_reference is a fictional, hypothetical automotive BMS development project grounded in foxBMS. Every ASIL value, hazard, safety goal, item, stakeholder, use case and test record in the synthetic_reference profile belongs to that fictional project. No ASIL determination, hazard analysis or safety concept shown here is a determination for the real foxBMS product, and nothing in this document transfers a requirement, a limit or a classification from one profile to the other.

How to navigate this document

  • Every artifact has an anchor of the form id="art-<profile>-<artifact id>". The profile is part of the anchor because the same artifact identifier exists in both profiles as two different records by corpus design; a single un-namespaced anchor could not address both.
  • A bare identifier in prose is hyperlinked to the as_is record when one exists and otherwise to the synthetic_reference record. Where both exist, the text says so, so a reader never mistakes one profile's record for the other's.
  • Every link registry entry has an anchor of the form id="lnk-<profile>-<link id>" and every coverage-matrix row an anchor id="cov-<profile>-<requirement id>".
  • Each section is a collapsible <details> block. Diagrams are rendered client-side; with scripting or a network unavailable, the Mermaid source stays readable as text and no other part of the document depends on a diagram rendering.

Regeneration is deterministic: every collection is iterated in sorted order, embedded data is serialised with sorted keys, and the template is fixed. The only field that may differ between two runs against an unchanged corpus is the data-generated-at attribute in this file's <head>, which carries the wall-clock time of the run. The integrity check generates the document a second time into a temporary directory and byte-compares the two after normalising that one attribute; every other byte must match or the check fails.

Item Definition

FB2-SAF-ITE-000001 — Item definition: the hypothetical 400 V traction battery monitoring and control unit of Project Northcell (Part 3 item)

Record classItem definition

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Item nameTraction battery monitoring and control unit (BMS), 400 V class

Item purposeMonitor the cell voltages, cell temperatures and pack current of a 400 V lithium-ion traction battery, keep every cell inside its safe operating area, and control the high-voltage contactors that connect and disconnect the battery, so that no cell leaves its safe operating area without the item having detected the condition and acted within a bounded time.

This item is fictional. The record's own item_identity.fictional flag is true. It describes a hypothetical automotive BMS project, not a real product.

vehicle platformHypothetical 400 V passenger BEV programme, 96S4P pack, one BMS master board plus four monitoring slaves

development stageSeries production intent. The corpus describes this project; no such vehicle, pack or programme exists.

reference implementationThe foxBMS 2 platform as read at commit 308028fb, used as the reference implementation whose measured behaviour the concept is grounded in. The real foxBMS 2 project is a research and development platform and is not this item.

grounding noteEvery statement about what the item does is a statement about the hypothetical project. Statements about what the real foxBMS sources do are source_observed and live in the as_is profile, never in this record.

In scope

  • Cell voltage, cell temperature and pack current acquisition, validation and publication
  • Safe operating area monitoring, debounce and classification
  • Measurement plausibility and redundancy checking
  • Contactor and precharge sequencing and feedback supervision
  • Fault management, severity handling, latching and persistent logging
  • Independent hardware voltage monitoring and its own actuation path
  • Configuration and calibration data that defines the safe operating area
  • The communication interfaces whose compromise could defeat a safety requirement

Out of scope

  • Thermal runaway arising from cell chemistry or damage that no E/E function can prevent
  • Mechanical protection of the pack (venting, enclosure, crash structure)
  • Charger and inverter control strategies
  • Vehicle-level crash isolation decisions
  • Production line and end-of-line test execution (documented, not performed here)
  • Field service execution and end-of-life recycling execution
  • Functional safety of the external current sensor and insulation monitoring device

Operating modes

ModeNameEntry conditionExit conditionSafe state in this mode
MOD-001INITIALISATIONSupply voltage within range and reset released.All configured data structures initialised and self-checks passed.Contactor drivers held de-energised. The item cannot command the contactors closed in this mode under any circumstance.
MOD-002STANDBYSelf-checks passed and the vehicle controller has not requested a current flow.A current-flow request is accepted, or a safety reaction is required.Contactor drivers de-energised; monitoring fully active.
MOD-003PRECHARGEA current-flow request is accepted and the pack voltage is below the precharge threshold.Pack voltage within tolerance of the bus voltage, or precharge timed out.If the precharge path is interrupted the item opens the precharge contactor and returns to STANDBY. It must never close string-plus on an incomplete precharge.
MOD-004CLOSED / CURRENT FLOWPrecharge complete and string-plus closed.A safety reaction, a state request to OPEN, or supply loss.This is the mode where the safe state is genuinely mode-dependent. Opening the contactors removes propulsion from a moving vehicle, so the item must distinguish a condition that is unsafe to continue from one that is merely degraded, and must not apply the FAULT reaction to a degraded condition.
MOD-005DEGRADEDA diagnosis entry whose severity permits continued operation with reduced capability.The degraded condition clears, or a condition requiring the full safe state arises.Capability is reduced and the reduction is indicated to the vehicle controller. The item must not enter DEGRADED for a condition that is a safety-goal violation.
MOD-006FAULTA diagnosis entry whose severity requires the safe state.The condition is acknowledged and cleared by an authorised service action only.All high-voltage contactors open, charging disabled, fault logged. This mode is latched: it is not left by the fault disappearing.
MOD-007COMMISSIONINGA maintenance pin or service tool asserts commissioning.The service session ends and the pin is removed.Contactor actuation inhibited unless an explicit, logged commissioning command is present. Open-circuit sensor inputs must not be interpreted as cell excursions.

Operational situations

SituationDescriptionIn/outCorpus argument for the decision
OS-001Vehicle parked, charger connected, mains present, pack at rest. The item is fully active and supervises the pack.includingThe charging case is the situation in which overvoltage happens most readily and in which a single cell may sit at the top of its range while the pack average looks normal. Excluding it would remove the situation the safety goal was written for.
OS-002Vehicle in motion, pack discharging, traction requested.includingIn this situation opening the contactors removes propulsion while the vehicle is moving. The safe state is therefore mode-dependent, and a blanket 'open on any fault' rule would be unsafe for a different reason. This situation is the reason the functional safety concept states its fault reaction per mode rather than once.
OS-003Vehicle in motion, regenerative braking, pack charging under load.includingRegeneration raises cell voltage under load, so the overvoltage detection path is exercised in a situation where opening the contactors is also disruptive.
OS-004Post-crash, high-voltage system possibly damaged, pack state unknown, insulation possibly lost.includingAfter a crash the item may be the only thing that knows whether the pack is energised. Its behaviour must be defined even though the environment is outside its specified range.
OS-005Production line, item not yet installed in a pack, cables not connected.includingThe commissioning mode is when open-circuit inputs and unconnected sensors are normal. A monitor that treats every open input as a cell at zero volts will produce false reactions in exactly this situation.
OS-006Workshop service, item removed from the pack, diagnostic tool connected.includingA service technician connecting a tool is the most likely route by which an external actor reaches the item's communication interfaces.
OS-007Storage and transport of the pack, not in a vehicle, not on a charger.excludingNo electrical function of the item is active, so no hazardous event attributable to the item arises. Excluded from the item's operational situations and addressed by the transport requirements of the pack integrator instead.
OS-008Post-decommissioning, pack dismantled for recycling.excludingThe item is destroyed or removed before this point. The hazard is handled by the recycler's own assumptions, recorded in the decommissioning record.
OS-009Workshop, item powered on a service supply, one measurement channel degraded by component drift or damage while the pack is otherwise healthy.includingA degrading channel is the situation in which the item's normal disagreement checks begin to fire on a pack that is not actually at a limit. Whether the item degrades gracefully or escalates to the safe state is decided here, and an item that escalates is safe and unusable. This situation is included for exactly that reason.

Interfaces to other safety-related items

Other itemInterface descriptionAssumption dependenceEffect if the assumption fails
Vehicle high-voltage safety monitor (the vehicle-level item that judges whether a collision or an insulation fault requires the pack to be isolated)The vehicle-level monitor asserts the interlock line and receives the item's state and insulation-related diagnosis.That the vehicle-level monitor is itself functional-safety qualified and that its assertion is not defeatable by the item.A pack insulation fault could persist with the contactors closed, or the item could open the contactors in a collision where keeping the pack energised is required for first-responder operation.
Battery cell supplier's cell-protection function (embedded in the protection circuit of each cell)The cell protection circuit disconnects a cell on its own overvoltage condition, independently of the item.That the cell protection circuit's threshold and timing are known to the item's integrator and are compatible with the item's own limits.The cell protection circuit could act before the item detects the condition, producing an unexplained capacity loss, or could fail to act at all in a cell whose protection is defeated, in which case the item is the only remaining barrier.

Misuse and service assumptions

AssumptionKindWho may violate itMitigation or declaration
The item is commissioned by a trained technician using the documented commissioning procedure.serviceAny person with physical access to the master board, which in a production vehicle is anyone who can reach the battery enclosure.The COMMISSIONING mode inhibits contactor actuation and is entered only on an explicit assertion, so an uncommissioned board cannot be energised by accident. This mitigates; it does not remove the assumption, and the service instructions record states the assumption explicitly.
Safe operating area limits are never raised beyond the cell chemistry's own limits to make a test pass or a driveability target.misuseAnyone with write access to the configuration, including the hypothetical project's own engineers.The limit set is part of the configuration baseline, and changing it is a controlled change requiring a safety impact analysis. No such analysis exists in this corpus, so the control is declared and not demonstrated.
The pack is not opened or serviced by the end user.maintenanceThe vehicle owner, and any party the owner permits.Declared as an assumption, not as a control. The item cannot enforce it; a high-voltage service restriction in the vehicle documentation is the assumed external measure.
At end of life the pack is handled by a certified recycler who treats a pack as energised until proven otherwise.recyclingA recycler who does not follow the declared procedure.Declared and carried into the decommissioning record as an end-of-life assumption with its control stated; the item itself contributes nothing to end-of-life safety once removed from the vehicle.

Stakeholder Needs

FB2-SYS-NED-000001 — Stakeholder need: the pack manufacturer shall not lose usable capacity through false safety reactions

Record classStakeholder need

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Need identifierFB2-SYS-NED-000001

Stakeholder{"fictional": true, "stakeholder_class": "pack_manufacturer", "stakeholder_description": "Fictional pack manufacturer of the hypothetical 400 V programme. Buys the item as a component into a pack it has designed and validated itself, and is accountable for the pack's usable energy and its own cell safety case.", "stakeholder_id": "STK-001"}

Need statementA pack manufacturer integrating the item shall be able to charge a healthy pack to its declared full state and discharge it to its declared minimum without the item reducing the pack's usable energy, and shall be able to state the delivered capacity against the declared capacity for warranty purposes.

Origin of the need{"elicitation_evidence": [], "elicitation_method": "assumption_declaration", "elicited_from": "the hypothetical programme's own design assumption set, declared by the author", "is_a_real_elicitation": false}

RationaleA safety function that reacts to a healthy pack is a cost the pack manufacturer carries and the driver experiences as a shortened range. The pack manufacturer therefore needs the reaction to be specific, not merely safe. This need is in genuine tension with the debounce strategy: every millisecond of debounce added to suppress false reactions is milliseconds taken from the detection latency the safety goal needs. The need is ranked first because the tension is the single most consequential design trade in the item and because the party that pays for a wrong resolution of it is not the party that makes the decision. It conflicts with the detection-latency need carried by the safety goal, which is stated there and not here.

Priority{"rank": 1, "rationale": "A safety function that reacts to a healthy pack is a cost the pack manufacturer carries and the driver experiences as a shortened range."}

FB2-SYS-NED-000002 — Stakeholder need: on a degradation the item shall retain a usable capability rather than escalate immediately

Record classStakeholder need

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Need identifierFB2-SYS-NED-000002

Stakeholder{"fictional": true, "stakeholder_class": "end_user_driver", "stakeholder_description": "Fictional end-user driver of the hypothetical vehicle. Not a technical stakeholder; cannot read a diagnosis entry and will not be shown one.", "stakeholder_id": "STK-002"}

Need statementWhen a measurement channel degrades, the item shall continue to supervise and control the pack with reduced capability and shall announce the reduction, rather than opening the contactors on the first detected disagreement.

Origin of the need{"elicitation_evidence": [], "elicitation_method": "assumption_declaration", "elicited_from": "the hypothetical programme's own design assumption set, declared by the author", "is_a_real_elicitation": false}

RationaleThe need is the difference between a serviceable vehicle and an immobilised one. An item that escalates every degradation to a safe state is not unsafe; it is unusable, and an unusable safety function gets disabled, overridden or removed by whoever is frustrated by it, which is the more likely outcome in the field. The need is therefore as much about the survival of the safety function as about capability. It is tightly coupled to the false-reaction need: a degraded mode that is too permissive reintroduces the false-reaction problem in a harder form, because a degraded channel is exactly the case where the item's normal checks are weakened.

Priority{"rank": 2, "rationale": "The need is the difference between a serviceable vehicle and an immobilised one."}

RationaleThis is the need that the master prompt's warning about mode-dependent safety behaviour makes unavoidable: disconnecting a battery during traction removes propulsion, so the reaction that satisfies the safety goal is itself a change in the vehicle's behaviour that a person has to live with. A driver who is cut off without an explanation will assume the worst and may attempt a restart sequence, which puts them back into contact with a pack the item has just isolated for a reason. The need is ranked second because it is the need most likely to be lost when the engineering is dominated by the reaction latency question.

Priority{"rank": 2, "rationale": "This is the need that the master prompt's warning about mode-dependent safety behaviour makes unavoidable: disconnecting a battery during traction removes propulsion, so the reaction that satisfies the safety goal is itself a change in the vehicle's behaviour that a person has to live with."}

FB2-SYS-NED-000004 — Stakeholder need: the vehicle manufacturer shall receive the item's state and limits and shall not be able to talk the item out of a safety decision

Record classStakeholder need

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Need identifierFB2-SYS-NED-000004

Stakeholder{"fictional": true, "stakeholder_class": "service_technician", "stakeholder_description": "Fictional service technician who commissions the item and services it in the workshop. Trained to the documented procedure and to nothing else.", "stakeholder_id": "STK-004"}

Need statementThe item shall publish its state, its limits and its fault condition to the vehicle manufacturer's control unit, and shall act on that control unit's state requests only when doing so is consistent with the item's own safety evaluation.

Origin of the need{"elicitation_evidence": [], "elicitation_method": "assumption_declaration", "elicited_from": "the hypothetical programme's own design assumption set, declared by the author", "is_a_real_elicitation": false}

RationaleThe vehicle manufacturer owns the vehicle-level safety case and needs enough of the item's state to integrate with it, and needs the item not to become a hazard to that case through an unhandled request. The two halves are in tension: an item that ignores requests cannot support vehicle features, and an item that honours them can be steered into a state its own monitoring has already judged unsafe. The need resolves the tension in one direction only - the item's own evaluation wins - and that direction is a deliberate asymmetry, not a neutral one.

Priority{"rank": 3, "rationale": "The vehicle manufacturer owns the vehicle-level safety case and needs enough of the item's state to integrate with it, and needs the item not to become a hazard to that case through an unhandled request."}

FB2-SYS-NED-000005 — Stakeholder need: a trained service technician shall be able to commission and service the item without being able to energise it incorrectly

Record classStakeholder need

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Need identifierFB2-SYS-NED-000005

Stakeholder{"fictional": true, "stakeholder_class": "end_of_line_tester", "stakeholder_description": "Fictional end-of-line test operator at the fictional pack plant who fits the item to a pack and commissions it before the pack ships.", "stakeholder_id": "STK-005"}

Need statementA service technician following the item's documented commissioning and service procedure shall be able to complete every step in the order given, and shall not be able by any sequence of the documented steps to leave the item able to command the contactors closed with unconnected or open-circuit sensor inputs.

Origin of the need{"elicitation_evidence": [], "elicitation_method": "assumption_declaration", "elicited_from": "the hypothetical programme's own design assumption set, declared by the author", "is_a_real_elicitation": false}

RationaleThe technician is the stakeholder with the least ability to recover from a mistake and the most opportunity to make one, because the procedure is executed on an item that is not yet trusted and therefore attracts improvisation. The second half of the need - the negative one - is the load-bearing part: a procedure that merely works is not enough, because the failure mode that matters is the one the procedure does not contemplate. This need also carries the item's commissioning-mode design requirement, which is why the mode exists at all.

Priority{"rank": 4, "rationale": "The technician is the stakeholder with the least ability to recover from a mistake and the most opportunity to make one, because the procedure is executed on an item that is not yet trusted and therefore attracts improvisation."}

2. System Requirements and Safety Concept

2. System Requirements and Safety Concept

The system level: what can go wrong, what must be achieved, how the concept achieves it, and the requirements derived from it. Technical (TSR), functional-safety (FSR), security (SEC), system (SYR) and management (SCO) requirement records all appear here, because they are all derived from or bound to the safety goals rather than allocated to software. Software requirements appear in section 4.

StatementThe BMS shall detect cell voltage limit violations and open all HV contactors within the fault tolerant time interval (FTTI = 100 ms) to prevent cell overvoltage/undervoltage hazardous events, with a target diagnostic test interval of 10 ms, a target contactor mechanical opening time of 30 ms (FB2-PRM-000005 / FB2-ASM-006) and a resulting 40 ms from the fault request to feedback-confirmed contactor open (FB2-SAF-FSR-000003).

Fault tolerant time interval{"note": "The interval this goal allocates is not defined here. It is the value of parameter FB2-PRM-000004 (ftti_ms = 100 ms, tolerance 100..100, calibrated by safety analysis against the HARA), and this field binds to it so that the ftti budget consistency checker resolves the interval from the parameter registry rather than from a literal restated on the record. fault_tolerant_time_interval_ms and timing_budget.total_ftti_ms remain on the record because other records and the published safety concept read them; the checker requires every declaration to agree with the bound parameter, so a drift in any of them is reported rather than resolved in favour of whichever value it happens to read first.", "parameter_ref": "FB2-PRM-000004"}

FB2-SAF-FSC-000001 — Functional Safety Concept: allocation of the cell-voltage safety goal to the architectural elements of the item

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Concept identity

Concept stagefunctional_safety_concept

Scope statement{"boundary_argument": "The scope is the set of failures the item can cause or detect-and-react to. Every element inside the boundary can produce the hazardous event by failing to report an overvoltage, failing to report it in time, or failing to open the contactor. Every element outside the boundary either cannot produce the event at all, or produces it through a route that passes back into one of the inside elements (for example a converter that overdrives a cell produces an overvoltage, which AR-001 then detects and AR-004 then reacts to, so the requirement lands inside the boundary even though the cause does not). The argument is drawn at the item's electrical interfaces, not at its functions, because the item's functions are chosen by the integrator and its interfaces are constrained by the chemistry.", "inside_safety_scope": ["Acquisition, validation and age-stamping of cell voltage and cell temperature", "Safe-operating-area monitoring, debounce, classification and the latched reaction", "Measurement plausibility and redundancy evaluation", "Contactor and precharge sequencing, actuation and feedback confirmation", "The independent hardware monitor and its own actuation path", "Supply and watchdog supervision as a barrier", "The integrity of the internal data path, to the extent that a forged or stale value could defeat a detection"], "outside_safety_scope": [{"element": "Thermal runaway from cell chemistry", "hazard_class": "inherent_battery_hazard_outside_fuSaS_scope", "why_outside": "A property of the cells, not of an E/E system. No requirement in this concept can prevent it, and pretending otherwise would inflate the ASIL of the item over a hazard it does not reach."}, {"element": "Mechanical protection of the pack", "hazard_class": "inherent_battery_hazard_outside_fuSaS_scope", "why_outside": "Venting and enclosure are mechanical. Their adequacy is the pack integrator's safety case."}, {"element": "Converter and charger control strategy", "hazard_class": "external_system_behaviour", "why_outside": "The item publishes limits and assumes they are respected (FB2-ASM-003). A converter that ignores them is an external-system behaviour failure, and the item's response to it is the protective disconnect already specified."}, {"element": "Vehicle-level crash isolation policy", "hazard_class": "external_system_behaviour", "why_outside": "Whether a collision requires isolation is a vehicle-level decision. The item supervises the interlock it is given."}, {"element": "Production programming and end-of-line test execution", "hazard_class": "production_or_service_process", "why_outside": "A lifecycle process, not a function. A wrongly configured item is a production escape, and it is handled by the production records, not by a functional requirement."}, {"element": "Electromagnetic robustness of the item under the full test level", "hazard_class": "environmental", "why_outside": "An environmental property. The concept assumes a level of robustness and does not claim to establish it."}]}

Safety goals addressed[{"allocation_statement": "The goal's objective - detect a cell voltage limit violation and reach the safe state, all contactors open, within the FTTI - is split across five of the six architectural elements below, and no single element is accountable for the whole objective. AR-001 owns detection of the condition; AR-002 owns the decision that the condition is confirmed; AR-003 owns carrying the decision to the actuator without it ageing or being forged; AR-004 owns commanding and confirming the contactor state; AR-005 owns an independent, second detection and actuation path that does not pass through any of the above. AR-006 owns only supply integrity and is explicitly not allocated any part of the goal's objective, which is why it can fail without defeating the goal.", "asil": "ASIL_D", "safety_goal_id": "FB2-SAF-SGO-000001"}]

Safety strategies{"degraded_operation": [{"capability_kept": "Monitoring at a higher rate, charge and discharge within reduced limits, contactor control retained", "capability_removed": "Full-rate charge and discharge, and the ability to claim the item is healthy", "degraded_mode": "Derated charge and discharge with enhanced monitoring", "duration_limit": "Until the degraded condition is cleared by service or exceeds the vehicle's own derating time limit", "entry_condition": "A diagnosis entry whose severity permits operation but forbids full-rate transfer", "user_indication": "The degraded state is published to the vehicle control unit so the driver is told the pack is restricted"}, {"capability_kept": "Contactor control and a coarser measurement set", "capability_removed": "Fast detection on the degraded channel", "degraded_mode": "Reduced-rate monitoring after a measurement-path degradation", "duration_limit": "Until service; a degraded channel is not cleared by the condition disappearing", "entry_condition": "Plausibility or redundancy detects a disagreement between channels", "user_indication": "Published to the vehicle control unit"}], "fault_detection": [{"coverage_claim": "Single-bit and double-bit errors in the transferred word", "coverage_claim_evidence": ["FB2-HW-TSR-000001 requires the front end to detect a single-bit error on every transfer; no measurement of that coverage exists in this corpus.", "FB2-VER-TMS-000001 and FB2-VER-EXE-000001 exercise the software path; the front end's own error-detection capability is not exercised by them."], "detection_time_budget_ms": 2, "detects": "A corrupted or mis-addressed cell-voltage transfer on the slave link", "element_id": "AR-001", "mechanism": "Front-end error-detection code on every measurement transfer"}, {"coverage_claim": "Front-end gain, offset and open-sense-line failures", "coverage_claim_evidence": ["FB2-SAF-FSR-000001 names plausibility and redundancy as the mitigation; Item-related assumptions[{"assumption": "A cell can leave its safe operating area at any time without warning, and the item will observe it as a voltage outside the configured limit.", "consequence_if_false": "If a cell failed in a way that stayed inside the limit while being dangerous (a chemistry failure at nominal voltage), every requirement in the concept would be satisfied and the hazard would still occur. Assumption referencesFB2-ASM-001: Lithium-ion cell chemistry with nominal voltage 3.7V, operating range 2.5V-4.2V
FB2-ASM-002: Thermal runaway initiates at cell voltage > 4.3V and temperature > 60°C
FB2-ASM-003: Vehicle charger respects BMS charge current limits communicated via CAN
FB2-ASM-004: AFE SPI communication latency < 5 ms (including DMA transfer and PEC validation)
FB2-ASM-005: Cell voltage measurement noise follows Gaussian distribution with sigma <= 5 mV
FB2-ASM-006: Contactor mechanical opening time <= 30 ms (worst case) at -40°C to +85°C
FB2-ASM-007: SBC (FS85xx) watchdog is independent of main MCU and can trigger contactor opening
FB2-ASM-008: Independent hardware voltage monitor (ASIL B) can be implemented with separate voltage dividers, comparator, and contactor drive
FB2-ASM-011: FreeRTOS task scheduling provides deterministic execution with worst-case latency < 2 ms for high-priority safety tasks

Record limitations

  • limitations: This concept is synthetic and describes a hypothetical programme. It establishes no property of the real foxBMS project and asserts no ASIL capability.; No diagnostic coverage figure in this concept is measured. Every one is either a requirement-side claim, an analytical estimate on an assumed noise distribution, or an assumption about a component that this corpus has not measured.; The independence of the hardware monitor is assumed (FB2-ASM-008), not demonstrated. An independent-monitor concept that had been analysed for common-cause failure would state which failures it does and does not cover; this one states that no such analysis exists in the corpus, which is why the dependent-failure analysis FB2-SAF-ANL-000003 exists and is referenced rather than replaced.; This concept does not verify anything. Verification is planned and, where a fixture exists, executed, in the FB2-VER-* records; none of that evidence is product evidence.; The architecture is a high-level functional decomposition. It says what each element is accountable for and not how any of them is built, and it does not establish that the elements as described can be built within the stated timing.; Human approval of this concept is pending. No functional-safety expert has confirmed it, and an automated review pass is not the independent confirmation an ASIL D concept requires.
  • lifecycle_status_note: Set to the value above because no human has reviewed or approved this record. `automated_review_status` below refers to corpus automation (schema, link, provenance and consistency checks run by docs/artifacts/tools/corpus.py) and is not a statement about engineering validity, organisational independence or human confirmation.

Hardware/software allocation[{"allocated_requirements": ["FB2-HW-TSR-000001", "FB2-HW-TSR-000002", "FB2-SW-SWR-000001"], "allocated_responsibility": "The front end, its dividers, the isolation and the measurement chain are hardware; the transfer scheduling, the error-code validation and the publication with age stamping are software.", "allocated_to": "split", "element_id": "AR-001", "reason_for_the_split": "The accuracy and the error-detection capability are properties of the analogue chain and cannot be implemented in software, while the guarantee that a value carries its age and was validated is a property of the software and cannot be implemented in the front end. Splitting the two means neither side has to be trusted with what only the other can do."}, {"allocated_requirements": ["FB2-SW-SWR-000002", "FB2-SW-SWR-000001"], "allocated_responsibility": "Limit comparison, debounce, plausibility, redundancy, severity classification and the request for the safe state.", "allocated_to": "software", "element_id": "AR-002", "reason_for_the_split": "These are decisions over a data set that only exists in memory. There is no hardware implementation of a debounce that would be cheaper or safer here; the risk in this element is algorithmic and is managed by software freedom from interference, not by moving the logic into silicon."}, {"allocated_requirements": ["FB2-SW-SWR-000001", "FB2-SAF-SEC-000003", "FB2-SAF-SEC-000004"], "allocated_responsibility": "The shared store, its consistency mechanism, the age stamp on every entry and the message-level integrity and freshness of the external interface.", "allocated_to": "software", "element_id": "AR-003", "reason_for_the_split": "The integrity mechanism is a protocol and a dispatch policy. The hardware can guarantee that bytes arrive; only the software can decide which bytes are acceptable."}, {"allocated_requirements": ["FB2-HW-TSR-000003", "FB2-SW-SWR-000003"], "allocated_responsibility": "The safe base controller, its independent watchdog and the coil drivers are hardware; the state machine that decides when to command them and the feedback interpretation are software.", "allocated_to": "split", "element_id": "AR-004", "reason_for_the_split": "The actuation must work when the MCU has stopped, so the watchdog and the final driver stage are hardware (FB2-ASM-007). The decision to act is a software decision, and keeping the decision in software while the final stage is in hardware is what makes the watchdog meaningful: if the software hangs, the hardware still opens the contactors."}, {"allocated_requirements": ["FB2-HW-TSR-000004", "FB2-SAF-FSR-000004"], "allocated_responsibility": "The independent dividers, the comparator, its threshold reference and its own actuation output. Entirely hardware.", "allocated_to": "hardware", "element_id": "AR-005", "reason_for_the_split": "The whole point of this element is that it does not pass through the main MCU. Any software in it would share the failure domain it exists to escape. The functional requirement FB2-SAF-FSR-000004 describes its objective; the technical requirement is FB2-HW-TSR-000004."}, {"allocated_requirements": ["FB2-HW-TSR-000002"], "allocated_responsibility": "Supply supervision, the watchdog window and the reset path. Entirely hardware.", "allocated_to": "hardware", "element_id": "AR-006", "reason_for_the_split": "It must act when the software cannot run, which rules out any software dependency."}]

Hardware interfaces and assumptions[{"basis": "FB2-ASM-008, a declared assumption. It is the assumption the whole ASIL D allocation leans on and it is not demonstrated anywhere in this corpus.", "consequence_if_unmet": "The independent monitor becomes a second channel with the same failure modes as the first. Two agreeing channels would then be read as corroboration when in fact they are one channel twice, and the safety goal would have no surviving barrier against an AR-001 to AR-004 common-cause failure.", "element_id": "AR-005", "interface_or_assumption": "AR-005 shares no MCU, no supply rail and no communication path with AR-001 to AR-004."}, {"basis": "FB2-ASM-007, grounded in the observed watchdog arrangement in the pinned source. The independence is read out of the source; its behaviour over the full temperature and supply range is not measured.", "consequence_if_unmet": "A software hang leaves the contactors in their last commanded state and the software-side fault reaction never runs. The hardware monitor AR-005 would then be the only remaining path, at 50 ms against a 100 ms interval, which leaves room but no margin for anything else.", "element_id": "AR-004", "interface_or_assumption": "The safe base controller's watchdog is independent of the main MCU and can actuate the contactors on its own."}, {"basis": "The requirement FB2-HW-TSR-000001 states the figure. No measurement of it exists in this corpus; the closest related record is a hardware test measure whose execution is blocked for lack of target hardware.", "consequence_if_unmet": "A total error comparable to the margin between the configured limit and the last cell that must remain in service would make the limit boundary ambiguous, and the 1 mV threshold accuracy the decision function relies on would be unattainable.", "element_id": "AR-001", "interface_or_assumption": "The cell input network and its calibration deliver the stated 1.5 mV total error over the full temperature range."}, {"basis": "Engineering assumption. The observed source contains supply supervision and a supply-related diagnosis entry, but no characterisation of the rails.", "consequence_if_unmet": "A supply collapse faster than the watchdog window produces an uncontrolled shutdown of the contactor drivers. Whether that is safe depends on the driver's fail state, which this corpus does not record.", "element_id": "AR-006", "interface_or_assumption": "The supply rails stay inside their specified range for long enough for the watchdog to act deliberately."}, {"basis": "FB2-SAF-FSR-000001 states a freshness criterion of 30 ms and FB2-SAF-SEC-000003 requires freshness verification on the external interface. The internal store's age handling is not separately specified in any record.", "consequence_if_unmet": "A decision is taken on a value from an earlier acquisition period. Diagnostic coverage assumptions[{"claimed_coverage": "Every single-bit error in a transferred cell-voltage word is detected before the value reaches the decision function.", "common_cause_note": "A fault in the front end's own computation that produces a wrong but correctly coded value is a measurement error, not a transfer error, and is covered by plausibility rather than by this mechanism.", "independence_assumption": "The check is performed in AR-001, the same element that produced the value. A front end that both corrupts a value and forges its code is not covered.", "justification": "A parity or CRC of the width the front end specifies, applied to every word. The detection property of such a code is a property of its polynomial and width, which is a matter of arithmetic rather than of measurement.", "justification_basis": "analytical_model", "mechanism": "Front-end integrity code on every measurement transfer (AR-001)", "verification_record_refs": ["FB2-VER-TMS-000001", "FB2-VER-EXE-000001"]}, {"claimed_coverage": "A false reaction rate below 1e-6 per hour for Gaussian measurement noise with sigma 5 mV, while detection of a true violation costs at most two acquisition periods.", "common_cause_note": "The debounce protects against noise. It does not protect against a systematic offset in the measurement chain, which a debounce makes worse: a real offset produces a confident, repeated violation.", "independence_assumption": "Consecutive samples are treated as independent. Correlated noise would change the rate materially and nothing in this corpus establishes independence.", "justification": "For a threshold placed several sigma from the noise mean, the probability that two consecutive samples both fall beyond the threshold is the square of the single-sample tail probability. At 20 Hz that yields the stated rate. The arithmetic is a property of the assumed distribution, which is itself an assumption (FB2-ASM-005), so the figure is conditional on that assumption and is not a measurement of the real item.", "justification_basis": "analytical_model", "mechanism": "Debounce on the limit comparison (AR-002)", "verification_record_refs": ["FB2-VER-TMS-000005", "FB2-VER-EXE-000005"]}, {"claimed_coverage": "A front-end gain error, an offset error and an open sense line are detected because each produces a value outside the plausible envelope or in disagreement with the redundant channel.", "common_cause_note": "A shared supply, a shared reference or a shared configuration source defeats redundancy without producing a disagreement. The dependent-failure analysis exists precisely because this cannot be dismissed by assertion.", "independence_assumption": "The redundant channel must be genuinely independent of the channel it checks. FB2-SAF-ANL-000003 records that analysis and FB2-SAF-ANL-000004 records the freedom-from-interference argument; neither quantifies the residual common-cause exposure.", "justification": "The mechanisms are self-evident from their design intent and are implemented in the observed source. What is NOT established is their coverage: the corpus contains no fault-injection campaign that quantifies which injected faults are detected and which are not, and no plausibility limit is expressed as a diagnostic-coverage figure.", "justification_basis": "synthetic_assumption", "mechanism": "Measurement plausibility and redundancy comparison (AR-002)", "verification_record_refs": []}, {"claimed_coverage": "A welded contactor is detected within 100 ms of the commanded state disagreeing with the feedback.", "common_cause_note": "A loss of the auxiliary return line is indistinguishable from a welded contactor at the interface, and the item must resolve that ambiguity conservatively.", "independence_assumption": "The auxiliary contact path and the coil drive path share no element that can fail open in both.", "justification": "The auxiliary contacts are wired independently of the coil drive, so a welded contactor produces a state disagreement that no failure of the drive path can mask. This is a wiring argument, and its validity depends on the wiring being as described, which no inspection record in this corpus establishes.", "justification_basis": "analytical_model", "mechanism": "Contactor auxiliary feedback and weld detection (AR-004)", "verification_record_refs": ["FB2-VER-TMS-000003", "FB2-VER-EXE-000003"]}, {"claimed_coverage": "Every cell the main measurement chain monitors is also measured by the independent divider network and compared against its own threshold.", "common_cause_note": "A common supply rail or a common reference between AR-005 and AR-001 would make the two channels agree in the presence of a shared fault and would defeat the independence the ASIL D argument relies on. FB2-SAF-ANL-000003 records this as an open question.", "independence_assumption": "Assumed (FB2-ASM-008): separate dividers, separate comparator, separate supply and no communication with the main chain. Nothing in this corpus demonstrates it, and the absence of a demonstration is itself the largest open assumption of the ASIL D allocation.", "justification": "The requirement FB2-HW-TSR-000004 now states this coverage as 100 percent of the main chain's monitored cell set, which is decidable on hardware: measure which cells the independent divider network reaches and divide by which cells the main chain reaches. The previous wording of this entry carried the requirement's own disjunction ('all monitored cells, or a representative subset of at least 50%') forward, which was not a measurable coverage statement; finding FB2-REV-FND-000027 recorded that and the requirement has now been revised. The 100 percent figure is STILL not demonstrated by anything in this corpus: it is a requirement, and its feasibility as a full per-cell network remains the open assumption FB2-ASM-008. The basis is therefore still an assumption rather than a measurement or an analytical model, and this entry must not be read as evidence of coverage.", "justification_basis": "synthetic_assumption", "mechanism": "Independent hardware threshold monitor (AR-005)", "verification_record_refs": []}]

FTTI and timing budget{"allocation": {"afe_acquisition_ms": 25, "contactor_command_ms": 5, "contactor_mechanical_ms": 30, "database_publish_ms": 3, "fault_classification_ms": 2, "feedback_verification_ms": 5, "pec_validation_ms": 2, "soa_limit_check_ms": 5, "spi_transfer_ms": 5, "sys_state_transition_ms": 3}, "allocation_to_element_id": {"afe_acquisition_ms": "AR-001", "contactor_command_ms": "AR-004", "contactor_mechanical_ms": "AR-004", "database_publish_ms": "AR-001", "fault_classification_ms": "AR-002", "feedback_verification_ms": "AR-004", "pec_validation_ms": "AR-001", "soa_limit_check_ms": "AR-002", "spi_transfer_ms": "AR-001", "sys_state_transition_ms": "AR-002"}, "arithmetic_check": {"margin_ms": 15, "serial_sum_ms": 85, "statement": "25 + 5 + 2 + 3 + 5 + 2 + 3 + 5 + 30 + 5 = 85 ms of serial work. The fault-tolerant time interval is 100 ms, so the margin available is 100 - 85 = 15 ms, and this concept allocates exactly 15 ms of it. The budget therefore closes with no deficit. This concept originally recorded that allocation as a deliberate departure from FB2-SAF-SGO-000001, which then carried a 20 ms margin and therefore a 105 ms total against the same 100 ms interval. That departure no longer exists: FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 now records the 15 ms margin as well, so the two records agree and the safety goal's budget closes. The 105 ms was not rounded to 100 ms; the margin was corrected to the value the interval admits, and 85 + 15 = 100. The reaction chain at the end of the budget is 5 ms coil command + 30 ms mechanical opening + 5 ms feedback verification = 40 ms, and FB2-SAF-FSR-000003 now states those three points separately as 5 ms, 35 ms and 40 ms, so the requirement and this allocation agree. The independent path AR-005 has its own 50 ms budget and does not draw on this one; the two budgets are alternatives, not a sum."}, "ftti_ms": 100}

Record limitations

  • limitations: This concept is synthetic and establishes no ASIL capability for any real product. Human approval is pending and no independent functional-safety confirmation exists.; No diagnostic coverage figure here is measured. Two entries are analytical models whose validity rests on stated assumptions, two are synthetic assumptions with no evidence at all, and one is a wiring argument that no inspection record supports.; The technical safety requirements listed here are the ones that already exist in the corpus. This concept does not derive new technical requirements, so parts of the allocation above are covered by requirement text written before the allocation was made. That is a real limitation and it is why the AR-005 coverage claim could not be improved here.; The timing budget is an allocation of intent. It is not a worst-case analysis: no WCET, no queueing analysis and no measured execution time for any of its ten entries exists in this corpus. A budget that is internally consistent is not the same as a budget that is met.; The independent hardware monitor has no schematic, no BOM and no analysis in this corpus. Its allocation to AR-005 is a statement of where the concept wants it, not a description of a circuit that exists.; No requirement in this concept has been verified against the real product. The existing executions that touch these elements are synthetic fixtures or blocked records; see the FB2-VER-EXE-* set.

CONTROLS PRESENT, each read from the pinned source: (1) the EMAC hardware filters on the destination MAC address, configured for every channel with EMAC_MAC_ADDRESS_MATCH (src/app/driver/emac/emac.c:238), so a frame not addressed to the ECU's MAC is dropped before it reaches the CPU; (2) a frame-type filter is applied before a frame is transferred (NetworkInterface.c:285), and it is active rather than compiled out, because the project sets ipconfigETHERNET_DRIVER_FILTERS_FRAME_TYPES to 1 (src/os/freertos/freertos-plus/freertos-plus-tcp/source/include/FreeRTOSIPConfig.h:275), which selects the real eConsiderFrameForProcessing path at NetworkInterface.c:73 rather than the unconditional eProcessBuffer alternative at NetworkInterface.c:71; (3) the received length is bounded against ipTOTAL_ETHERNET_FRAME_SIZE before the frame is copied (NetworkInterface.c:237) and the destination buffer is allocated to that received length (NetworkInterface.c:226). CONTROLS ABSENT, recorded as observations and deliberately not inflated into a threat: (1) there is no minimum-length check on the receive path at the driver layer. The 60-byte minimum NIC_ETH_MIN_FRAME_BYTES (NetworkInterface.c:79) is applied only in NIC_FormatBuffer on the transmit path (NetworkInterface.c:163-165) and is never applied to an incoming frame, so a short received frame is not rejected here; (2) there is no ingress rate limit, no per-source frame accounting, and no broadcast or multicast policy control anywhere in this driver; (3) the receive path processes only single-buffer-descriptor frames and does not chain descriptors for a fragmented frame, which the code states in a comment and leaves as a TODO (NetworkInterface.c:289-295), so its effect is to bound which frames are processed rather than to validate them. IMPORTANT BOUND ON CONTROL 1, which is the reason this asset does not reduce any threat: a destination-MAC match filter is NOT an access control against an attacker who is already present on the segment. Such an attacker chooses the destination MAC and therefore passes the filter; the filter only excludes traffic originating off-segment. It must not be read as authentication, and there is no credential check, no integrity check, no replay protection and no rate limit anywhere on this path. The MAC filter therefore does not weaken the attacker precondition of THR-001 or THR-002, both of which already require a peer present on the segment. For that reason no new threat ID was derived from this asset, and that decision is recorded in method.limitations rather than left implicit.", "interface": "IEEE 802.3 Ethernet frame ingress at the MAC layer, on the same physical link as AST-001. Threats[{"affected_safety_goals_or_requirements": ["FB2-SAF-SGO-000001"], "attack_vector": "Adjacent host on the same Ethernet link, or any host with a routed path to 169.254.107.24, opens TCP to port 7. The handshake succeeds unconditionally.", "description": "Unauthenticated, unencrypted TCP session establishment on the echo server. ETH_ListenForConnection calls FreeRTOS_socket/freeRTOS_bind/FreeRTOS_listen and then loops on FreeRTOS_accept (src/app/application/ethernet/ethernet.c:255, :276-283, :286-293). Between accept and the hand-off of the connected socket there is no check of the peer address (clientAddress is filled by accept as an output parameter and never inspected; pParameters is explicitly discarded at :248), no credential exchange, no cryptographic handshake, and no connection-rate limit. No TLS library is present anywhere in the master communication stack. The MAC/PHY ingress path in front of this service (AST-009) was also read: it filters on the destination MAC address (src/app/driver/emac/emac.c:238) and applies a frame-type filter before handing a frame up (NetworkInterface.c:285, active in this configuration per src/os/freertos/freertos-plus/freertos-plus-tcp/source/include/FreeRTOSIPConfig.h:275), but neither is a security control against a peer on the segment, because the destination MAC is chosen by the sender and the frame-type filter discards protocol types rather than authenticating a peer. This threat therefore holds at the MAC layer as well as at the TCP application layer.", "honest_unknowns": ["Whether any deployment puts a routable interface in front of this segment is unknown.", "No attempt was made to connect to port 7 on hardware; reachability is inferred from the code and the configured address only.", "Whether FreeRTOS-Plus-TCP applies any connection-level rate limit of its own was not audited.", "The EMAC does filter on the destination MAC address and does apply a frame-type filter before a frame is handed up (AST-009), but neither was tested on hardware and the frame-type filter is a vendored-stack mechanism whose coverage of this configuration was read from the configuration macro rather than exercised. Neither is an authentication control, and the destination-MAC filter is satisfied by any sender on the segment, so neither reduces the attacker precondition stated in attack_vector."], "impact": "The peer obtains an established TCP session to the master and an on-target task that services it. The capability granted is limited to the echo service: the received bytes are echoed and are never written to the internal database, so this does NOT by itself permit actuation or measurement manipulation. The concrete impact is occupancy of the single echo-server queue slot and of an echo-server task (see THR-003), and the ability to use the ECU as a fixed-target TCP reflector (see THR-002).", "likelihood_impact_reasoning": "Impact on confidentiality, integrity and availability of battery data is low, because the evidenced service is a pure echo and the code path from accepted socket to database does not exist. Impact on availability is medium, because the connection occupies a resource that has no admission control (THR-003). Likelihood is deployment-dependent and cannot be rated from source: the interface uses a link-local address with no DHCP and no routed path in the default configuration, so an external attacker requires either physical/logical presence on the link or a deployment that routes the subnet. The corpus cannot resolve this and does not assume either way.", "mitigation_ids": ["MIT-001", "MIT-002"], "observed_in_pinned_source": true, "origin": "source_observed", "residual_risk": "medium", "residual_risk_justification": "With MIT-001 and MIT-002 implemented in the hypothetical project, an unauthenticated peer is rejected before a task is created, so residual likelihood is governed by the strength of the credential store and by network segmentation, neither of which is defined in this corpus. The rating is therefore bounded to 'the exposure is removed but the compensating segmentation controls are unspecified', and is explicitly not a statement that the residual risk is acceptable.", "source_refs": ["FB2-SRC-COD-000057", "FB2-SRC-COD-000062", "FB2-SRC-COD-000063", "FB2-SRC-COD-000078", "FB2-SRC-COD-000080", "FB2-SRC-COD-000081", "FB2-SRC-COD-000083"], "target_asset_ids": ["AST-001", "AST-002", "AST-009"], "threat_id": "THR-001"}, {"affected_safety_goals_or_requirements": [], "attack_vector": "A third party that can direct traffic at the ECU's IP and port 7 receives that traffic back, giving the ECU a stable, non-rewriting reflector endpoint and a liveness oracle for the segment.", "description": "The echo server is a byte-reflecting service with a fixed, well-known port and a fixed link-local address. ETH_EchoServerInstance receives N bytes into rxBuffer (src/app/application/ethernet/ethernet.c:175) and returns those same N bytes to the peer (:184-193) with no parsing, no filtering and no content check.", "honest_unknowns": ["No traffic measurement was performed; the absence of amplification is an argument from reading the send loop, not from measurement."], "impact": "The ECU can be used as a fixed-target reflector. IMPORTANT BOUND: the evidenced echo is one-for-one in the send direction (receivedBytes in, receivedBytes out), so this is NOT a volumetric amplification primitive as the code is written. AssumptionsThe analysis assumes the code read at commit 308028fb is the code that is built and deployed. If a downstream integration adds a protocol on the serial receive queue, or a write-capable service on the network interface, the corresponding threats (THR-006, THR-007) must be re-analysed before those ratings may be reused.; The analysis assumes the configured values are the effective values: ETH_ECHO_SERVER_PORT_NUMBER = 7, ETH_ECHO_SERVER_BACKLOG = 1, ETH_ECHO_SERVER_RECEIVE_TIMEOUT = portMAX_DELAY (src/app/application/config/ethernet_cfg.h:90, :85, :94), ipconfigTCP_MSS = 536 (src/os/freertos/freertos-plus/freertos-plus-tcp/source/include/FreeRTOSIPConfig.h:294), and ETH_DEFAULT_DEBUG_MESSAGE_SIZE = 30 (src/app/application/ethernet/ethernet.c:80, which is defined in the module itself rather than in a configuration header). The 30 is the length of the fixed greeting banner and the 536 is the length of the receive buffer; they are separate constants at separate locations and neither is derived from the other. No build was performed and no binary was inspected.; The analysis assumes ipconfigHAS_DEBUG_PRINTF is not enabled. It is not defined in the project's FreeRTOSIPConfig.h, so it takes the default ipconfigDISABLE, which reduces FreeRTOS_debug_printf to a no-op. Under that configuration the latent unterminated-buffer read at ethernet.c:189 is compiled out. If a variant enabled debug printf, that statement would no longer hold and the defect would become live. This is recorded as a configuration-dependent latent defect, NOT as a vulnerability, and no out-of-bounds read is claimed to be reachable in the evidenced configuration.; The analysis assumes the diagnosis engine reports entries as configured. DIAG_ID_CAN_RX_QUEUE_FULL is configured DIAG_EVALUATION_ENABLED with DIAG_SEN_EVENT_1; whether the reporting path is itself functional at runtime was not tested.; The analysis assumes the CAN identifiers in tools/dbc/foxbms.dbc correspond to the receive table compiled into the target. That correspondence was not re-derived for this record.; Reachability of the Ethernet segment, the CAN bus and the serial line is assumed to be a deployment property outside the repository. No rating in this record depends on a specific reachability assumption, and none is asserted.

Assumption referencesFB2-ASM-011: FreeRTOS task scheduling provides deterministic execution with worst-case latency < 2 ms for high-priority safety tasks

This record's statement specifies 'a debounce of 2 consecutive violations within 100 ms' and 'classify violations within 5 ms of data availability', and FB2-PRM-000006 records soa_debounce_count = 2, which is where those figures come from. The source does not implement them. src/app/application/soa/soa.c implements a three-tier MOL/RSL/MSL comparison with no counter in the SOA module at all, and the debounce that does exist is the DIAG occurrence counter, configured at 50 events for the MSL tier (diag_cfg.c:126). There is no 5 ms classification figure in either bms_cfg.h or diag_cfg.c. The statement, the acceptance criteria and the parameter registry have NOT been edited, because the statement is a requirement and a requirement that does not match the implementation is a different finding from a missing fault reaction, and closing it requires a decision about which of the two is authoritative. It is recorded here so that a reader of this reaction is not left believing that the 100 ms debound and 5 ms classification are implemented behaviour. Also unresolved: no measurement of the counter threshold, the delay or the state transition exists in this corpus.", "profile_basis": "as_is", "reaction": "Set the corresponding diagnosis entry, and if that entry's configured severity is DIAG_FATAL_ERROR, drive the battery state machine into the latched error state, which opens the HV contactors. Only the MSL tier reaches that path: DIAG_ID_CELL_VOLTAGE_OVERVOLTAGE_MSL and DIAG_ID_CELL_VOLTAGE_UNDERVOLTAGE_MSL are configured DIAG_FATAL_ERROR, while the RSL tier is DIAG_WARNING and the MOL tier is DIAG_INFO, and both non-MSL tiers carry DIAG_DELAY_DISCARD (src/app/engine/config/diag_cfg.c:126-131). An excursion into the RSL or MOL band therefore produces a recorded diagnosis and no contactor opening, which is a real graded reaction and not an omission.", "reaction_time_budget_basis": "DIAG_DELAY_200ms from diag_cfg.c:126 and diag_cfg.c:129. This is the delay between the entry becoming active and the state request, and it is the delay for a DIAG_FATAL_ERROR entry, not the whole reaction. The debounce in front of it is a count, not a time: DIAG_SEN_EVENT_50 is a threshold of 49 and DIAG_GetDiagnosisEntryState at src/app/engine/diag/diag.c:287-301 activates the entry when occurrenceCounter > 49. The evaluations are driven once per BMS_Trigger from src/app/application/bms/bms.c:913, and the BMS task period is BMS_STATEMACHINE_TASK_CYCLE_CONTEXT_MS = 10 ms (src/app/application/config/bms_cfg.h:100), so 50 evaluations is of the order of 500 ms and the state request follows roughly 700 ms after a sustained excursion. That figure is read off the configuration, not measured.", "reaction_time_budget_ms": 200, "triggered_by": "A cell voltage crossing BC_VOLTAGE_MAX_MOL_mV, BC_VOLTAGE_MAX_RSL_mV or BC_VOLTAGE_MAX_MSL_mV, or the corresponding minimum limits, evaluated in SOA_CheckVoltages() at src/app/application/soa/soa.c:89-131. Whether the crossing produces a reaction at all, and which one, is decided by the configured severity of the corresponding entry, not by the comparison."}

FB2-SAF-FSR-000002 — FSR: SOA Voltage Limit Monitoring with Debounce

Record classRequirement (FSR)

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

This identifier also exists in the as_is profile as a different record: FB2-SAF-FSR-000002.

Statement

The BMS shall monitor each cell voltage against configured minimum and maximum limits with a debounce of 2 consecutive violations within 100 ms, and classify violations within 5 ms of data availability, triggering FAULT state request on confirmed violation.

Rationale

SOA monitoring must detect limit violations fast enough to meet FTTI. Debounce of 2 violations in 100 ms balances false positives vs detection latency (statistical analysis shows < 1e-6 false positive rate for Gaussian noise sigma=5mV).

FB2-SAF-FSR-000003 — FSR: Contactor Opening on SOA Violation

Record classRequirement (FSR)

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

This identifier also exists in the as_is profile as a different record: FB2-SAF-FSR-000003.

Statement

The BMS shall command all HV contactors to open within 5 ms of a FAULT state request from SOA/DIAG, shall reach the mechanically open state within 35 ms of that request, and shall confirm the commanded state from the auxiliary feedback within 40 ms of that request.

Rationale

Contactor opening is the primary risk reduction measure. The chain is three segments, and each segment has its own bound: the coil command within 5 ms, the mechanical opening within 30 ms (FB2-PRM-000005, FB2-ASM-006, worst case over -40 to +85 degC), and the auxiliary feedback confirmation within a further 5 ms. From the FAULT request the mechanically open point is therefore 5 + 30 = 35 ms and the feedback-confirmed point is 5 + 30 + 5 = 40 ms, which is the same 40 ms the safety goal allocates (contactor_command 5 + contactor_mechanical 30 + feedback_verification 5) and which fits inside the 100 ms fault-tolerant time interval with the 15 ms margin FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 now records. The earlier wording of this record stated a 30 ms threshold against a 35 ms rationale, which contradicted its own 5 ms coil-command criterion and the safety goal's 40 ms; the three figures were true of three different points on one chain and the defect was that a single criterion carried the value belonging to another point. Finding FB2-REV-FND-000024.

FB2-SAF-FSR-000004 — FSR: Independent Hardware Voltage Monitor

Record classRequirement (FSR)

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Statement

The item shall maintain, as a second barrier to the ASIL D cell-voltage safety goal FB2-SAF-SGO-000001, a cell-overvoltage detection and HV-contactor-opening capability that is independent of the main measurement, decision and command path, so that a failure confined to the main path does not remove the overvoltage reaction; the capability shall be allocated ASIL B and shall produce its contactor-open request within 50 ms of the overvoltage it detects.

Rationale

Provides freedom from interference for the ASIL D safety goal: a main-path-only reaction leaves no tolerance in the 100 ms interval. As allocated in FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 the main path is 85 ms (25 acquisition + 5 SPI + 2 PEC + 3 publish + 5 SOA check + 2 classification + 3 state transition + 5 coil command + 30 mechanical + 5 feedback), which leaves 15 ms. At the 40 ms upper tolerance of FB2-PRM-000005 the contactor chain is 5 + 40 + 5 = 50 ms and the main path is 95 ms, leaving 5 ms. If detection waits one full acquisition period of FB2-PRM-000003 (50 ms) instead of the 25 ms allocated, the main path is 85 - 25 + 50 = 110 ms and overruns the interval. A parallel ASIL B path with its own 50 ms budget (FB2-PRM-000007) is therefore the second barrier, not an optimisation. This functional requirement states the safety intent and the behaviour that decides it; the hardware obligation and the structural independence properties are specified by FB2-HW-TSR-000004, and the system-level separation is specified by FB2-SYS-SYR-000005.

FB2-SAF-SEC-000001 — SEC-000001: Authenticated and confidential transport for externally reachable network services

Record classRequirement (SEC)

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Statement

The BMS master software shall not service any externally reachable network session until the peer has been authenticated by a cryptographically sound mechanism, and shall protect the confidentiality and integrity of all session data after authentication.

Rationale

A network service that accepts an unauthenticated peer is exposed to anyone who can route a packet to its interface, and every later control in the security concept is then built on an unauthenticated channel. The requirement is written ahead of the hypothetical project's planned diagnostic and configuration service (TARA threat THR-007) as well as the service that exists today, so that the higher-consequence service is not designed without authentication. confidentiality is required in addition to authentication because a reflecting service on a fixed interface is usable by a third party as a stable traffic-reflection endpoint even when it grants the peer no access to internal data (TARA threat THR-002).

Real source presenceControl ABSENT. The real foxBMS 2 master's only network service is a plain-TCP echo server: src/app/application/ethernet/ethernet.c:255 creates an AF_INET/SOCK_STREAM/IPPROTO_TCP socket, :276-281 binds it, :288 calls FreeRTOS_accept, and the accepted socket is handed to a task at :292 with no credential exchange, no peer-address check and no cryptographic handshake. The peer address is captured by accept as an output parameter and never inspected, and the endpoint parameter is explicitly discarded at :248. No TLS or equivalent cryptographic library is present in the master communication stack. Anchor FB2-SRC-COD-000057.

The real foxBMS 2 master's only network service is a plain-TCP echo server: src/app/application/ethernet/ethernet.c:255 creates an AF_INET/SOCK_STREAM/IPPROTO_TCP socket, :276-281 binds it, :288 calls FreeRTOS_accept, and the accepted socket is handed to a task at :292 with no credential exchange, no peer-address check and no cryptographic handshake. The peer address is captured by accept as an output parameter and never inspected, and the endpoint parameter is explicitly discarded at :248. No TLS or equivalent cryptographic library is present in the master communication stack. Anchor FB2-SRC-COD-000057.

FB2-SAF-SEC-000002 — SEC-000002: Bounded connection admission and per-service resource budget

Record classRequirement (SEC)

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Statement

The BMS master software shall bound the resources consumed by any network service by enforcing, for every service, a hard cap on concurrently serviced connections, a finite receive timeout, a per-connection byte budget, and a deterministic close of any connection that exceeds its budget, and shall raise a diagnosis entry on every admission refusal and every budget breach.

Rationale

A service with unbounded connection resources can be made to stop serving legitimate peers by a peer that requires no special capability. In the real source the relevant conditions are present in combination: the listen backlog is a compile-time constant of 1, the accept loop hands every accepted socket to a single-deep queue with a zero block time and discards the enqueue result, and the receive timeout is portMAX_DELAY, so a connected peer that sends nothing blocks its service task indefinitely. The requirement also requires the refusal to be diagnosable, because a silently discarded overflow cannot be distinguished from normal operation during field analysis (TARA threats THR-001, THR-003).

FB2-SAF-SEC-000003 — SEC-000003: Message-level integrity and freshness for safety-relevant CAN messages

Record classRequirement (SEC)

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Statement

For every CAN identifier whose payload influences a safety function, the BMS master software shall verify, before the payload is passed to its receive callback, a rolling counter that establishes freshness, an integrity check that a bus peer cannot produce without the shared secret, and a data-length code matching the length expected for that identifier; a frame failing any of the three shall be rejected before the callback is invoked and shall raise a diagnosis entry.

Rationale

Dispatch on identifier alone means that any node that can transmit on the bus can present a frame that the master accepts as genuine, because an identifier is not a credential. This is the highest-consequence exposure identified in the TARA, because the affected identifiers carry the cell voltage, cell temperature and pack current signals on which the safety requirements depend. All three checks are required and none is redundant: without the counter an authentic frame can be replayed indefinitely; without the integrity check the counter is forgeable by any bus peer; without the length check a short frame can be interpreted as if trailing bytes were meaningful (TARA threat THR-005, TARA mitigation MIT-004).

FB2-SAF-SEC-000004 — SEC-000004: Framing, integrity and authorisation on the serial link, and demotion of the XOFF/XON control bytes

Record classRequirement (SEC)

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Statement

The BMS master software shall accept a serial (SCI/UART, RS485) frame only after an explicit length field has been validated against the received byte count and an integrity field has been verified, shall pass only authenticated frames to the application layer, and shall treat the XOFF and XON byte values as ordinary payload unless they arrive inside a frame that has already been authenticated.

Rationale

The serial receive path in the real source has no framing, no length field, no integrity field and no authorisation, and it treats two arbitrary byte values as privileged commands: any 0x13 on the line suppresses the master's transmission, and any 0x11 restores it, with no authentication and no diagnosis. A single byte placed on the line is therefore sufficient to alter the master's behaviour on that link, which is a control-injection condition even though the current consequence is limited. Framing and authentication are required together because an integrity field on an unframed stream can be forged or misaligned by the peer, and the control-byte clause is required because a value that acts as a command must not be reachable outside an authenticated frame (TARA threat THR-006, TARA mitigation MIT-005).

Real source presenceControl ABSENT. src/app/driver/uart/uart.c:163 arms a single-byte interrupt-driven receive into one static byte (declared at :108). In the receive interrupt at :244-263, the values 0x13 and 0x11 (defined at src/app/driver/uart/uart.h:68-69) are consumed at :247-250 to gate transmission, and every other byte is forwarded to a queue at :254 with the enqueue return value discarded, so overflow is silent and no diagnosis entry is raised. No framing, length validation, integrity field or authorisation exists anywhere on this path. A further absence is recorded honestly and constrains the impact rating: the application consumer of this queue is a stub — FTSK_RunUserCodeUart in src/app/task/config/ftask_cfg.c:330-338 contains only UART_HandleFlowControl() and OS_NotifyTake() and never calls UART_Read — so no application data path from the serial receive queue to the database was found, and the evidenced impact is confined to transmit suppression and silent overflow. This requirement MUST be re-derived if the hypothetical project connects a protocol to this queue. Anchors FB2-SRC-COD-000067, FB2-SRC-COD-000068, FB2-SRC-COD-000069, FB2-SRC-COD-000070, FB2-SRC-COD-000071.

FB2-SAF-SEC-000005 — SEC-000005: Cryptographically strong entropy for network security parameters, and governed third-party component management

Record classRequirement (SEC)

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Statement

The BMS master software shall derive the initial TCP sequence number and any other network security parameter from a cryptographically strong entropy source that is re-seeded at every boot from a source not fixed at build time; and the project shall maintain, under a named owner, an inventory of every third-party component in the target and in the commissioning toolchain, each entry carrying the evidence for its version, together with a scheduled process that checks that inventory against an authoritative advisory source and records the result.

Rationale

The two clauses address the two ways in which the item's security posture degrades without a code defect. The first: the real source derives the TCP initial sequence number from a single 32-bit state seeded with a build-time literal and advanced by a fixed multiplier plus a tick count, and the source itself annotates the generator as insufficient. A predictable initial sequence number removes a defence-in-depth layer of the TCP connection, so the entropy source must be sound before any authenticated protocol is layered on top of it. The second: an inventory that is never checked against an advisory source records what is present but says nothing about whether it is affected, and an inventory whose version evidence is guessed is worse than no inventory because it cannot be acted on (TARA threats THR-004, THR-008; TARA mitigations MIT-006, MIT-009).

FB2-SYS-SYR-000001 — SYR: every monitored cell voltage shall be acquired, validated and published with its age

Record classRequirement (SYR)

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Statement

The item shall acquire the voltage of every monitored cell, validate the integrity of every transferred value before it is used by any decision, and publish each validated value together with the age of the acquisition that produced it, at a rate of at least 20 acquisitions per second in every mode in which the item is monitoring.

Rationale

This is the system-level statement of what FB2-HW-TSR-000001 and FB2-SW-SWR-000001 together achieve. It is not a restatement of either: the hardware record states the measurement accuracy and the error-detection capability of the analogue chain, and the software record states the transfer scheduling and the publication latency. Neither states the age of the data, and the age is what makes every downstream timeout meaningful: a value without an age cannot be rejected for being stale, so a decision made on it may be acting on an acquisition from several periods earlier.
