FB2-SYS-SYR-000002 — SYR: the item shall enforce the configured safe operating area, and shall distinguish a recoverable measurement degradation from a limit violation

Record classRequirement (SYR)

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Statement

The item shall compare every monitored cell voltage against the configured maximum and minimum limits, shall require two consecutive violations within 100 ms before classifying a violation, and shall move to its degraded mode rather than to the safe state when a measurement channel's disagreement is explainable by a degradation within the declared plausibility envelope, escalating to the safe state only when the degradation removes the reference the item needs.

Rationale

The first half of this requirement restates the enforcement the safety goal needs. The second half is new at system level and is the boundary the stakeholder need FB2-SYS-NED-000002 depends on: the difference between a degraded item that stays usable and an item that disconnects on the first channel disagreement. Neither the existing SOA software requirement nor the plausibility requirement states that boundary, because in both cases the boundary is a question about the integrated item's behaviour rather than about one module's algorithm. The corpus records no numerical value for the degraded-to-fault boundary and this requirement deliberately does not invent one; it requires the boundary to exist and to be declared, which is what makes its absence visible.

FB2-SYS-SYR-000003 — SYR: the item shall reach and confirm the safe state within the fault-tolerant time interval, and shall latch the condition that required it

Record classRequirement (SYR)

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Statement

On a confirmed safe-operating-area violation the item shall open all high-voltage contactors, disable charging and log the fault within 100 ms of the condition becoming measurable, shall confirm the open state by auxiliary feedback, and shall not leave that state on the fault disappearing.

Rationale

The system-level statement of the safety goal's objective. It is written at this level because the obligation spans three allocated requirements - the software state machine, the hardware driver path and the hardware feedback path - and a requirement that any one of them could claim to satisfy would let the end-to-end timing go unstated. The figure here is the safety goal's own fault-tolerant time interval; the way that interval is spent is the technical safety concept's business, not this requirement's.

FB2-SYS-SYR-000004 — SYR: the fault reaction shall be selected by mode, and a degraded condition shall never be reacted to as if it were a safe-operating-area violation

Record classRequirement (SYR)

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Statement

The item shall select its reaction according to the mode it is in and the nature of the condition, shall reach the safe state on a confirmed safe-operating-area violation in every mode, and shall enter its degraded mode rather than the safe state on a condition that its own monitoring has classified as degraded. The item shall publish the mode it is in and the reason for any departure from normal operation.

Rationale

This requirement exists because the master prompt states that one contactor action is not unconditionally safe in every operating situation, and because the two other requirements in this set are silent about it. Opening the contactors in the traction mode removes propulsion; opening them in the charging mode removes a hazard; opening them in commissioning mode is not reachable at all. A requirement that says 'open the contactors on a violation' is therefore incomplete rather than merely conservative, because it does not say what the item does when the violation happens at speed.

FB2-SYS-SYR-000005 — SYR: the item shall include a hardware voltage monitor that can detect an overvoltage and open the contactors without the main microcontroller

Record classRequirement (SYR)

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Statement

The item shall include a cell-voltage monitor that measures through its own divider and comparator chain, holds its own threshold reference and its own supply, and commands the contactors open within 50 ms of detecting an overvoltage, using no processing resource, no supply rail and no communication path of the main microcontroller.

Rationale

The system-level statement of the independent path. The functional safety requirement FB2-SAF-FSR-000004 and the hardware requirement FB2-HW-TSR-000004 state the same intent in identical words, which is a defect in the corpus rather than in the design: two records at two different ISO 26262 levels cannot be the same sentence. This record separates them by saying what is technically required, namely the separation of supply, reference, computation and actuation, and it names the specific coupling that would defeat the independence if it existed. The independence is still an assumption (FB2-ASM-008); this requirement makes it explicit and checkable without pretending it has been checked.

FB2-SYS-SYR-000006 — SYR: pack current and cell temperature shall be acquired, plausibility-checked and supplied to the item's supervisory functions

Record classRequirement (SYR)

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Statement

The item shall acquire the pack current and the temperature of every monitored cell group, shall mark a measurement invalid when it cannot be trusted, and shall compare each valid value against the plausible operating envelope before using it in a supervisory decision.

Rationale

The safety chain in this corpus is entirely a cell-voltage chain: the hazard, the safety goal and all four functional safety requirements concern cell voltage. Current and temperature supervision are system-level requirements nonetheless, because the item publishes charge and discharge limits that the converter is assumed to respect (FB2-ASM-003), and a limit published from an untrustworthy measurement is not a limit. This requirement is stated as a system requirement rather than a safety requirement precisely because the corpus carries no hazard, no safety goal and no ASIL for the current and temperature paths. Recording it as a system requirement with no ASIL is the honest position; inflating it to match the cell-voltage chain would be an unsupported ASIL assignment.

FB2-SYS-SYR-000007 — SYR: the item shall publish its state and shall not accept a request that contradicts its own safety evaluation

Record classRequirement (SYR)

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Statement

The item shall publish its mode, its charge and discharge limits and its active fault condition to the vehicle control unit, and shall act on a state request from that unit only when the request is consistent with the item's own safety evaluation; where it is not, the item shall refuse the request and publish the refusal with its reason.

Rationale

The system-level statement of the integration contract with the vehicle manufacturer. It resolves the tension named in the stakeholder need FB2-SYS-NED-000004 in one direction and states the direction explicitly, because a requirement that said only 'the item honours state requests' would leave the safety case resting on the item being overridden cleanly, and 'cleanly' is not a property any record here establishes. The publication half is separated from the refusal half deliberately: publication is a capability the vehicle manufacturer needs in every mode, and refusal is a safety behaviour that only exists when the item has already judged something unsafe.

FB2-SYS-SYR-000008 — SYR: commissioning and service shall not permit the item to energise on unconnected or untrusted inputs

Record classRequirement (SYR)

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Statement

While the item is in its commissioning mode, no high-voltage contactor shall be commanded closed unless an explicit commissioning command is present, and an open-circuit or unconnected sensor input shall be diagnosed as such and shall not be interpreted as a cell at a limit; on leaving commissioning, the item shall return to a state in which no contactor actuation is possible without a current-flow request. Bytes received on a service link shall be acted upon only inside a validated, authenticated frame.

Rationale

The system-level requirement behind the commissioning mode, and the one that carries the service-class stakeholder need FB2-SYS-NED-000005 into the item's architecture. Its second half is deliberately a cybersecurity requirement appearing at system level: the framing and authorisation of the service link is a property of the integrated item's interfaces, not of one module, and the security requirement FB2-SAF-SEC-000004 constrains the same link from the other direction. Both halves exist because the failure they guard against is the one a production or service error produces, and no safety requirement in this corpus covers it.

FB2-HW-TSR-000004 — TSR: Independent Hardware Voltage Monitor

Record classRequirement (TSR)

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Statement

The hardware shall realise the ASIL B overvoltage reaction as a discrete chain separate from the main measurement chain: every cell monitored by the main chain shall be divided by a dedicated divider network into a comparator that holds its own overvoltage threshold reference on a supply rail not shared with the main chain, and the comparator output shall drive a contactor driver stage whose command is not sourced from the main microcontroller. No divider, reference, comparator, driver or supply of this chain shall be common with the main measurement or actuation chain, and the chain shall reach the contactor-open command within 50 ms of the overvoltage it detects. The contactors are common to both paths and are not part of this requirement. Allocated from FB2-SAF-FSR-000004 through FB2-SYS-SYR-000005 to architectural element AR-005 of FB2-SAF-TSC-000001.

Rationale

Hardware realisation of the second barrier required by FB2-SAF-FSR-000004, decomposed at system level by FB2-SYS-SYR-000005 and allocated to element AR-005 of FB2-SAF-TSC-000001. Freedom from interference for the ASIL D cell-voltage goal rests on this chain sharing no measurement, reference, supply or command resource with the main chain: as allocated in FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 the main path is 85 ms of the 100 ms interval, 95 ms at the 40 ms upper tolerance of FB2-PRM-000005, and 110 ms if detection waits one full acquisition period of FB2-PRM-000003 instead of the 25 ms allocated. Its own budget is 50 ms (FB2-PRM-000007) and it is an alternative to that path, not an addition to it.

FB2-SW-SIR-000001 — Software interface requirements: the acquisition and monitoring interfaces

Record classRequirement (REQ)

profile synthetic_reference · origin derived · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Statement

The acquisition and monitoring interfaces shall present the following to their consumers: (a) a request entry point whose result reports acceptance or rejection; (b) a completion query by which a consumer can determine whether the first measurement cycle has completed; (c) a string-addressed request whose argument range is bounded by the configured string count; and (d) a supervision entry point that is invoked on the 10 ms cycle and whose entire effect is delivered through the diagnosis module rather than through a return value.

Rationale

The requirements exist because the interface specifications analysed at the pinned commit show that this boundary has four properties a consumer must be able to rely on, and that none of them is stated by the interface itself. Without these requirements a consumer would have to read the implementation to learn them, which is what an interface requirement is supposed to prevent. The four properties are: a request result that distinguishes acceptance from rejection; a separate completion signal, because the request returns before the measurement exists; a bounded string argument, because the enforcement is an assertion in a wrapper rather than a returned error; and side-effect-only supervision, because the supervision entry points return nothing at all.

FB2-SW-SIR-000002 — Software interface requirements: the actuation interface

Record classRequirement (REQ)

profile synthetic_reference · origin derived · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Statement

The actuation interface shall present the following to its consumers: (a) a request entry point whose result reports whether the request was placed on a configured contactor; (b) a state read that returns an explicit indication when no such contactor exists rather than a stale or default state; (c) a feedback check whose entire effect is delivered through the diagnosis module; and (d) an argument range on every actuation request, bounded by the configured string count and excluding the undefined contactor type.

Rationale

The requirements exist because the analysed interface has two properties a consumer must be able to rely on and one it demonstrably lacks. The two are that the string and contactor-type arguments are bounded, and that a state read distinguishes 'no such contactor' from a real state. The third is the gap: the single negative return value is used both for a request that matched nothing and for a request that matched and could not be completed, so a consumer cannot tell a configuration error from a transient condition. Stating that as a requirement rather than leaving it as an observation is what makes the gap visible to a requirements process instead of to whoever happens to read the source.

FB2-SW-SIR-000003 — Software interface requirements: the communication and data-exchange interfaces

Record classRequirement (REQ)

profile synthetic_reference · origin derived · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Statement

The communication and data-exchange interfaces shall present the following to their consumers: (a) a transmit call whose result reports whether the frame was placed on the bus; (b) an identifier argument whose range is bounded by the identifier width the caller selected; (c) a data-block read whose result reports whether the request was accepted and which shall not be represented as returning the data; (d) a bounded maximum queue wait on that read; and (e) a single-consumer serialisation rule for concurrent access to the data blocks.

Rationale

These requirements exist because the two analysed boundaries behave differently in ways a consumer must know and cannot infer from a signature. The transmit interface has an explicitly unchecked identifier, recorded in the source as a deliberate non-assert, and its queue pump discards a frame when the retransmit queue is full. The data-exchange interface is asynchronous: it returns before the data exists, and its return value reports only whether the request was queued. A consumer of either would have to read the implementation to learn that, which is the situation an interface requirement exists to prevent.

FB2-SW-SIR-000004 — Software interface requirements: the platform-service and serial-bus interfaces

Record classRequirement (REQ)

profile synthetic_reference · origin derived · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Statement

The platform-service and serial-bus interfaces shall present the following to their consumers: (a) a masking entry point that states what it excludes and that rejects a nested entry; (b) a time base that states its unit and its resolution; (c) a serial read that reports a transfer which did not start as a failure rather than a success; (d) a lock that states its owner, its timeout and the consequence of a release that the caller does not hold; and (e) a transfer length parameter that is bounded against the destination buffer the caller supplies.

Rationale

These requirements exist because the analysed boundaries fail in ways a consumer cannot detect from the outside. The I2C read reports a skipped transfer as success when the bus is busy, so a caller can believe it holds data it does not have. The SPI lock has no owner, no timeout and no refusal on a spurious release, so a lost release is indistinguishable from a correct one and a refused claim carries no timing information. Two buffer-length parameters are explicitly unchecked by a decision recorded in the source. A masking entry point that cannot detect nesting is the third such case. None of these is visible in a signature, and all four are the kind of property an interface requirement exists to state.

FB2-SW-SIR-000005 — Triage of the seven unsatisfied software interface-requirement elements

Record classRequirement (REQ)

profile synthetic_reference · origin derived · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Statement

Seven element requirements across FB2-SW-SIR-000002, FB2-SW-SIR-000003 and FB2-SW-SIR-000004 are not satisfied by the implementation at 308028fb. This record gives each one a disposition. Four are unimplemented product behaviour the requirements correctly call for and the code does not provide (FB2-SW-SIR-000002-E, FB2-SW-SIR-000003-B, FB2-SW-SIR-000004-A, FB2-SW-SIR-000004-C). One is a mis-derived requirement that asks for more than the interface is for (FB2-SW-SIR-000004-D, a lock owner and timeout where a boolean flag is the whole design). One is satisfied only partially, on the documentation rather than the mechanism (FB2-SW-SIR-000004-B, a time base whose unit is documented but whose resolution is not). One is a documentation gap with a real safety consequence (FB2-SW-SIR-000004-E, unbounded transfer lengths). None of the seven is closed by this record and none of the four requirement records is rewritten.

Rationale

The interface-requirement family was authored by analysing the source and then stating what the interface would have to do for a consumer to rely on it. Seven of those statements are not met. The honest next step is to say, per requirement, whether the code is wrong, the requirement is wrong, or the code is half-right, and to name the engineering action. This record does that and stops there. In particular it does not restate any requirement to fit the code, because four of the seven are real gaps and rewriting them would convert a recorded product weakness into a green tick.

FB2-SW-SIR-000006 — Software interface requirements: the power-path, balancing, redundancy, insulation, ADC, DMA and SBC interfaces

Record classRequirement (REQ)

profile synthetic_reference · origin derived · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Statement

The power-path, plausibility, redundancy, balancing, ADC, DMA, SBC and insulation interfaces shall present the following to their consumers: (a) a switch-feedback read that distinguishes a closed contactor from a faulty feedback line and states a settling time; (b) a plausibility comparison that states its tolerance and that does not publish an averaged value it has just declared implausible; (c) a redundancy validation that identifies which quantity failed rather than returning one aggregate verdict; (d) a balancing interface that identifies the strategy that provides it; (e) a conversion sequence with a timeout and an observable state; (f) a transmit-status interface whose declared symbols have definitions; (g) a supervisor trigger that reports whether its watchdog was refreshed; and (h) an insulation trigger whose success return means the cycle did work.

Rationale

These eight boundaries were specified in this pass because the corpus already treats them as safety-relevant and the software-in-the-loop run already exercises them. What the specification of each boundary exposed is the same class of problem the earlier four interface-requirement records found: the interface promises less than a consumer needs, and the shortfall is not visible in a signature. A contactor feedback read returns the same value for a closed contactor and a broken feedback line. A plausibility check averages two measurements and publishes the average even when it has just rejected them. A redundancy check returns one verdict for every cell of every string. A conversion sequence can be stuck with no error state. Two declared transmit-status symbols do not exist. A watchdog refresh is invisible. None of that is a code defect in the ordinary sense; it is the absence of a stated contract, which is precisely what an interface requirement exists to put right.

FB2-SW-SWR-000002 — SWR: SOA Voltage Limit Monitoring

Record classRequirement (SWR)

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

This identifier also exists in the as_is profile as a different record: FB2-SW-SWR-000002.

Statement

The SOA module shall read cell voltages from database and compare against configured minimum (2.5V) and maximum (4.2V) limits with a debounce of 2 consecutive violations within 100 ms, and classify violations within 5 ms of data availability, triggering FAULT state request on confirmed violation.

Rationale

SOA monitoring must detect limit violations fast enough to meet FTTI. Debounce of 2 violations in 100 ms balances false positives vs detection latency (statistical analysis shows < 1e-6 false positive rate for Gaussian noise sigma=5mV).

Architecture Decisions

FB2-SW-DSN-000001 — Design: AFE Driver Architecture (LTC Family)

Record classArchitecture design

profile as_is · origin derived · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

TitleDesign: AFE Driver Architecture (LTC Family)

Design levelarchitecture

Engineering domainsoftware

Owner rolesw_engineer

Lifecycle statusreviewed

Variant applicabilityVAR-REF-001

Responsibilities

  • SPI/DMA communication with LTC AFEs
  • Command sequencing (wakeup, read, balancing)
  • PEC calculation and validation
  • Data conversion to mV/°C
  • Database publishing

Interfaces

InterfaceDirectionSignalsNotes
AFE_DATABASEoutputcell_voltages — uint16_t[], mV, range 0-5000, rate 20 Hz
cell_temperatures — int16_t[], 0.1°C, range -400-1500, rate 20 Hz
balancing_feedback — bool[], bool, range 0/1, rate 20 Hz		not specified in corpus
AFE_SPIbidirectionalspi_tx — uint8_t[], bytes, range 0-255, rate 1 MHz
spi_rx — uint8_t[], bytes, range 0-255, rate 1 MHz		not specified in corpus

Constraints

  • SPI clock ≤ 1 MHz (LTC6811 spec)
  • DMA buffer size: 256 bytes per slave
  • Task period: 100 ms (FreeRTOS task)
  • Stack usage: < 2 KB

Decisions

Recorded decisions[{"alternatives": ["Polling", "DMA", "Interrupt"], "decision_id": "DEC-AFE-001", "rationale": "Lowest CPU overhead for multi-slave reads", "selected": "DMA"}, {"alternatives": ["Single read all", "Split voltage/temp"], "decision_id": "DEC-AFE-002", "rationale": "LTC6811 requires separate commands", "selected": "Split voltage/temp"}]

FB2-SW-DSN-000001 — Design: AFE Driver Architecture (LTC Family)

Record classArchitecture design

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

TitleDesign: AFE Driver Architecture (LTC Family)

Design levelarchitecture

Engineering domainsoftware

Owner rolesw_engineer

Lifecycle statusbaselined

Variant applicabilityVAR-REF-001

Responsibilities

  • SPI/DMA communication with LTC AFEs
  • Command sequencing (wakeup, read, balancing)
  • PEC calculation and validation
  • Data conversion to mV/°C
  • Database publishing

Interfaces

InterfaceDirectionSignalsNotes
AFE_DATABASEoutputcell_voltages — uint16_t[], mV, range 0-5000, rate 20 Hz
cell_temperatures — int16_t[], 0.1°C, range -400-1500, rate 20 Hz
balancing_feedback — bool[], bool, range 0/1, rate 20 Hz		not specified in corpus
AFE_SPIbidirectionalspi_tx — uint8_t[], bytes, range 0-255, rate 1 MHz
spi_rx — uint8_t[], bytes, range 0-255, rate 1 MHz		not specified in corpus

Constraints

  • SPI clock ≤ 1 MHz (LTC6811 spec)
  • DMA buffer size: 256 bytes per slave
  • Task period: 100 ms (FreeRTOS task)
  • Stack usage: < 2 KB

Decisions

Recorded decisions[{"alternatives": ["Polling", "DMA", "Interrupt"], "decision_id": "DEC-AFE-001", "rationale": "Lowest CPU overhead for multi-slave reads", "selected": "DMA"}, {"alternatives": ["Single read all", "Split voltage/temp"], "decision_id": "DEC-AFE-002", "rationale": "LTC6811 requires separate commands", "selected": "Split voltage/temp"}]

TitleDetailed Design: LTC 6813-1 AFE measurement driver - internal units, PEC contract, transmission timing and error propagation

Design leveldetailed_design

Engineering domainsoftware

Owner rolesw_engineer

Lifecycle statusbaselined

Variant applicabilityVAR-REF-001

Responsibilities

  • Accept measurement and maintenance requests from the application layer and convert each into an LTC_STATEMACH_e state request against ltc_stateBase, returning whether the request was accepted (src/app/driver/afe/ltc/api/ltc_afe.c:86-140)
  • Advance one LTC 6813-1 state machine instance per call from the transmission and receive buffers held in LTC_STATE_s (src/app/driver/afe/ltc/6813-1/ltc_6813-1.c:833-2964)
  • Verify the LTC 6813-1 packet error code over every received block and record per-device validity in the error table (src/app/driver/afe/ltc/6813-1/ltc_6813-1.c:3838-3878)
  • Convert validated cell voltages and GPIO temperatures into the database and set the per-cell invalidCellVoltage bits from the error table rather than from a separate plausibility pass (src/app/driver/afe/ltc/6813-1/ltc_6813-1.c:597-654, 3110-3135)
  • Release the state machine from the SPI DMA completion interrupt that signals the end of a transmission (src/app/driver/afe/ltc/common/ltc_afe_dma.c:88-93)
  • Compute the CRC-15 packet error code used by the transmit and receive paths (src/app/driver/afe/ltc/common/ltc_pec.c:75-115)

Constraints

  • Transmission budget per command: LTC_TRANSMISSION_TIMEOUT is 10 and is added to LTC_STATE_s->commandDataTransferTime for each armed transition (src/app/driver/afe/ltc/6813-1/config/ltc_6813-1_cfg.h:162).
  • Daisy-chain frame geometry: LTC_N_BYTES_FOR_DATA_TRANSMISSION is 4 + 8 * LTC_N_LTC and LTC_N_LTC resolves to BS_NR_OF_MODULES_PER_STRING (src/app/driver/afe/ltc/common/config/ltc_cfg.h:68,79). LTC_CheckPec indexes the received buffer at 4 + (i * 8) through 11 + (i * 8), so the eight-byte stride is a hard coupling between the configuration macro and the integrity check.
  • PEC payload length is fixed: LTC_DATA_SIZE_IN_BYTES is 6 and LTC_CheckPec copies exactly six bytes into PEC_Check before computing (src/app/driver/afe/ltc/common/ltc_defs.h:87, src/app/driver/afe/ltc/6813-1/ltc_6813-1.c:3838-3878).
  • CRC table bound: LTC_PEC_PRECOMPUTED_TABLE_SIZE is 256 and the index is masked with LTC_PEC_ONE_BYTE_MASK (src/app/driver/afe/ltc/common/ltc_pec.h:66-68).
  • PEC accumulator bound: the accumulator is masked with LTC_PEC15_MASK (0x7FFF) and shifted left one, so it cannot exceed 0xFFFE (src/app/driver/afe/ltc/common/ltc_pec.h:70-72).
  • Per-device array bounds: the error table is indexed [BS_NR_OF_STRINGS][LTC_N_LTC] and every write to PEC_valid is inside a loop bounded by LTC_N_LTC (src/app/driver/afe/ltc/common/ltc_defs.h:74-81, src/app/driver/afe/ltc/6813-1/ltc_6813-1.c:3850-3876).
  • Invalidation granularity: a PEC failure invalidates exactly LTC_NUMBER_OF_CELL_VOLTAGES_PER_REGISTER cells, so the validity of one cell is decided by the integrity of a whole register (src/app/driver/afe/ltc/6813-1/config/ltc_6813-1_cfg.h:130, src/app/driver/afe/ltc/6813-1/ltc_6813-1.c:3110-3135).
  • Concurrency: AFE_DmaCallback runs in SPI DMA complete interrupt context and writes LTC_STATE_s->transmit_ongoing on the global ltc_stateBase, while AFE_SetTransmitOngoing and AFE_IsTransmitOngoing read and write the same field from task context. No critical section, mutex or atomic qualifier appears in src/app/driver/afe/ltc/common/ltc_afe_dma.c (src/app/driver/afe/ltc/common/ltc_afe_dma.c:77-93).…
  • Re-entrance: LTC_Trigger and BMS_Trigger both implement their own re-entrance counter (ltc_state->triggerentry) and return early when it is exceeded; the counters are independent and are not synchronised with each other.
  • Trigger cadence is build-configuration dependent, not fixed by the driver source. For the LTC family the build tool sets FOXBMS_AFE_DRIVER_TYPE_FSM because afe_driver_type defaults to "fsm" and the ltc branch does not change it, which places MEAS_Control in the 1 ms cyclic task; a dedicated-task configuration instead uses FTSK_TASK_AFE_CYCLE_TIME, which is 0 (src/app/task/config/ftask_cfg.c:246-25…
  • Interface identity restriction: AFE_DmaCallback asserts that spiIndex is one of exactly two SPI peripherals, so the driver cannot be moved to a third SPI peripheral without changing the assertion.

Failure Response

Failure modeDetectionReaction
Packet error code mismatch on one device in the daisy chainLTC_CheckPec recomputes the CRC-15 over the six data bytes of each device block and byte-compares the result against the two received PEC bytes (src/app/driver/afe/ltc/6813-1/ltc_6813-1.c:3838-3878)With LTC_DISCARD_PEC false, which is the pinned configuration, PEC_valid[stringNumber][i] is set false and LTC_CheckPec returns STD_NOT_OK. The caller passes that return value to DIAG_CheckEvent with pecDiagErrorEntry, so a diagnosis counter is raised. On the measurement path LTC_SaveVoltages then skips the store for that device and sets invalidCellVoltage true for LTC_NUMBER_OF_CELL_VOLTAGES_PER_REGISTER cells, so the stale value is not published as current.
PEC check compiled outThe LTC_DISCARD_PEC macro is a compile-time switch, so the condition is not detected at runtime; the alternative branch is visible in the source (src/app/driver/afe/ltc/6813-1/config/ltc_6813-1_cfg.h:106, src/app/driver/afe/ltc/6813-1/ltc_6813-1.c:3866)With LTC_DISCARD_PEC true the source sets PEC_valid true on a mismatch and leaves retVal at STD_OK, so a corrupted block is accepted and no diagnosis entry is raised. This is a configuration-dependent loss of the integrity check, not a runtime decision.
SPI operation returns a non-STD_OK value, including a transmission that does not complete within LTC_TRANSMISSION_TIMEOUTThe return value of the SPI operation is tested in LTC_CondBasedStateTransition, and independently LTC_Trigger skips its state switch while the armed timer has not expired or while AFE_IsTransmitOngoing is true (src/app/driver/afe/ltc/6813-1/ltc_6813-1.c:578-595, 833-869)LTC_CondBasedStateTransition calls DIAG_Handler with DIAG_EVENT_NOT_OK at DIAG_STRING impact for the current string and transitions to the caller-supplied state_nok/substate_nok pair. The enumerator LTC_STATEMACH_ERROR_SPIFAILED exists in the state set.
DMA completion interrupt arrives for a different SPI peripheralAFE_DmaCallback compares the completing spiIndex against SPI_GetSpiIndex(ltc_stateBase.ltcData.pSpiInterface->pNode) before clearing the flag (src/app/driver/afe/ltc/common/ltc_afe_dma.c:88-93)The flag is left set. No diagnosis entry is raised and no error is reported; the consequence is that LTC_Trigger continues to skip its state switch until the armed timer expires, after which it proceeds regardless of whether the transmission ever completed.
Out-of-range or null pointer reaches a driver entry pointFAS_ASSERT at the top of each entry point: string < BS_NR_OF_STRINGS on every request function, length > 0 and data != NULL_PTR on LTC_CalculatePec15, pLtcState != NULL_PTR on the DMA helpers and on LTC_TriggerThe assertion traps. There is no return path for a rejected argument and no error code for it.
Received cell voltage outside the plausible cell rangeThe driver performs no range check. The pinned source contains no plausibility comparison on the converted cell voltage in the LTC path; plausibility checking is a separate entry point, AFE_PlausibilityCheckVoltageMeasurementRange, declared in src/app/driver/afe/api/afe_plausibility.h, which is not invoked by LTC_SaveVoltagesNone in the driver. The value is stored and published with invalidCellVoltage false, so an out-of-range but correctly-PEC-checked value is published as valid.

FB2-SW-DSN-000005 — Detailed Design: SOA monitoring - tiered limit evaluation, limit-provider split, validity gating and the unimplemented slave-temperature entry point

Record classDetailed design

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

TitleDetailed Design: SOA monitoring - tiered limit evaluation, limit-provider split, validity gating and the unimplemented slave-temperature entry point

Design leveldetailed_design

Engineering domainsoftware

Owner rolesw_engineer

Lifecycle statusbaselined

Variant applicabilityVAR-REF-001

Responsibilities

  • Compare the per-string minimum and maximum cell voltage against three ordered over-voltage limits and three ordered under-voltage limits, raising or clearing one diagnosis entry per limit actually crossed (src/app/application/soa/soa.c:81-146)
  • Select the over-temperature and under-temperature limit set from the measured current direction, so that charging and discharging are evaluated against different thresholds, and raise or clear one diagnosis entry per limit crossed (src/app/application/soa/soa.c:148-269)
  • Gate the current evaluation on the per-string and pack validity bits before comparing against string, cell and pack current limits, and additionally test for current flowing on a string whose contactors report open (src/app/application/soa/soa.c:271-351)
  • Supply the numeric current limits and the current-on-open-string predicate to the evaluator, keeping the thresholds out of the evaluation code (src/app/application/config/soa_cfg.c:76-129)
  • Quantise a signed current to a three-valued flow direction so that a current below the rest threshold is neither charge nor discharge and is therefore exempt from every over-current limit (src/app/application/bms/bms.c:1697-1719)

Constraints

  • Evaluation period: all four entry points are called from BMS_Trigger at lines 913 to 916, and BMS_Trigger is called at the end of FTSK_RunUserCodeCyclic10ms. The SOA evaluation therefore runs at 10 ms in the pinned configuration (src/app/application/bms/bms.c:898-1691 and 913-916, src/app/task/config/ftask_cfg.c:258-282 and 280).
  • Loop bound: every evaluator iterates s from 0 to BS_NR_OF_STRINGS, which is 1 in the pinned configuration. The arrays indexed by s are declared with the same macro, so the loop cannot exceed the array (src/app/application/soa/soa.c:85 and 154 and 275, src/app/application/config/battery_system_cfg.h:109).
  • Comparison granularity: an entry is raised or cleared only when the value is on the far side of a named threshold, so the module's resolution is the spacing between MSL, RSL and MOL. In the pinned configuration that spacing is 80 mV between MOL and RSL and 50 mV between RSL and MSL on the over-voltage side, and 30 mV and 50 mV respectively on the under-voltage side.
  • Direction quantisation: a current whose magnitude is below BS_REST_CURRENT_mA, which is 200 mA, is reported as at rest and is therefore exempt from every current limit and from the current-on-open-string check. This is a resolution limit on the direction determination, not a filter on the current.
  • Sign convention dependency: the mapping from a signed current to a direction is inverted by BS_POSITIVE_DISCHARGE_CURRENT, so the meaning of a positive stringCurrent_mA is a configuration decision and the limit sets applied follow from it (src/app/application/bms/bms.c:1697-1719, src/app/application/config/battery_system_cfg.h:92).
  • Cell-current limit derivation: SOA_IsCellCurrentLimitViolated compares against BS_NR_OF_PARALLEL_CELLS_PER_CELL_BLOCK multiplied by the per-cell MSL macro rather than against a configured pack-level current, so changing the parallelism silently changes the cell limit while leaving the per-cell macro unchanged. With the pinned value of 1 the derivation is the identity.
  • Contactors crossed: SOA_IsCurrentOnOpenString reaches into the BMS layer for BMS_IsStringClosed and BMS_IsStringPrecharging, so the SOA evaluation is not a function of its arguments alone and its result depends on contactor state that the contactor driver updates on the same 10 ms pass (src/app/application/config/soa_cfg.c:116-129).
  • Ordering: the three populated evaluators run in the fixed order voltages, temperatures, current, and each raises or clears entries rather than accumulating, so within one pass a later evaluator cannot change an entry raised by an earlier one.
  • No debouncing in this module: every conclusion is published on the evaluation that reaches it. Any persistence across evaluations is a property of the diagnosis subsystem, not of the SOA module.

Failure Response

Failure modeDetectionReaction
Null structure pointer passed to any evaluatorFAS_ASSERT on the pointer at the top of each entry pointThe assertion traps. There is no return code and no skip path; the 10 ms pass stops at that call.
String index at or beyond BS_NR_OF_STRINGS reaches SOA_IsCurrentOnOpenStringFAS_ASSERT(stringNumber < BS_NR_OF_STRINGS) at the top of that providerThe assertion traps. The evaluator's own loop cannot produce such an index, so the only way to reach this is a caller outside the module.
String or pack current is invalidThe invalidStringCurrent and invalidPackCurrent bits read from the pack-values structureThe corresponding block is skipped. No entry is raised, so an invalid current cannot raise a fault; and no entry is cleared, so an entry raised by an earlier valid pass persists indefinitely while the reading stays invalid.
Diagnosis subsystem refuses an entryDIAG_Handler returns one of DIAG_HANDLER_RETURN_NOT_READY, DIAG_HANDLER_INVALID_TYPE, DIAG_HANDLER_RETURN_WRONG_ID or DIAG_HANDLER_RETURN_UNKNOWNIgnored, with one exception. Every call except the under-voltage MSL call discards the return. The under-voltage MSL call's return is compared against DIAG_HANDLER_RETURN_ERR_OCCURRED, so a refusal there suppresses DIAG_ID_DEEP_DISCHARGE_DETECTED rather than producing a spurious one.
A measured value lies outside the representable range of its element typeNot detected. The module casts the absolute current to uint32_t without checking, and applies no range check to voltage or temperature at all.None. The comparison proceeds on the cast value.
A slave temperature exceeds its limitNot detected. SOA_CheckSlaveTemperatures has an empty body.None. No slave-temperature limit is evaluated at any point.
A limit is violated but no action follows inside the moduleThe module's only action is to raise a diagnosis entry; it contains no contactor, no derating and no shutdown logicNone inside the module. The reaction to a raised entry is whatever the diagnosis subsystem and the BMS state machine are separately configured to perform, neither of which is in this module.

(from this record's constraints)
  • Loop bound: every evaluator iterates s from 0 to BS_NR_OF_STRINGS, which is 1 in the pinned configuration. The arrays indexed by s are declared with the same macro, so the loop cannot exceed the array (src/app/application/soa/soa.c:85 and 154 and 275, src/app/application/config/battery_system_cfg.h:109). (from this record's constraints)
  • Comparison granularity: an entry is raised or cleared only when the value is on the far side of a named threshold, so the module's resolution is the spacing between MSL, RSL and MOL. In the pinned configuration that spacing is 80 mV between MOL and RSL and 50 mV between RSL and MSL on the over-voltage side, and 30 mV and 50 mV respectively on the under-voltage side. (from this record's constraints)
  • Direction quantisation: a current whose magnitude is below BS_REST_CURRENT_mA, which is 200 mA, is reported as at rest and is therefore exempt from every current limit and from the current-on-open-string check. This is a resolution limit on the direction determination, not a filter on the current. (from this record's constraints)
  • Sign convention dependency: the mapping from a signed current to a direction is inverted by BS_POSITIVE_DISCHARGE_CURRENT, so the meaning of a positive stringCurrent_mA is a configuration decision and the limit sets applied follow from it (src/app/application/bms/bms.c:1697-1719, src/app/application/config/battery_system_cfg.h:92). (from this record's constraints)

(from this record's constraints)

FB2-SW-DSN-000006 — Detailed Design: contactor actuation and auxiliary feedback - registry, command/feedback split, lookup contract and the open-wire TODO

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

TitleDetailed Design: contactor actuation and auxiliary feedback - registry, command/feedback split, lookup contract and the open-wire TODO

Design leveldetailed_design

Engineering domainsoftware

Owner rolesw_engineer

Lifecycle statusbaselined

Variant applicabilityVAR-REF-001

Responsibilities

  • Hold the contactor registry: one entry per contactor carrying the commanded state, the last observed feedback, the feedback source kind, the owning string, the contactor type, the switch-peripheral channel and the preferred breaking direction (src/app/driver/config/contactor_cfg.h:107-121)
  • Translate a request to open or close a named contactor on a named string into a switch-peripheral channel request, and report whether the registry contained a matching entry (src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c:165-201)
  • Sample the auxiliary feedback of every contactor from whichever of the four configured feedback sources that contactor uses, and publish it into the registry (src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c:86-106)
  • Compare commanded state against sampled feedback per contactor and raise or clear one diagnosis entry per contactor type (src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c:125-163)
  • Gate the precharge-specific open and close calls on the string actually having a precharge contactor configured (src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c:203-221)
  • Open every contactor unconditionally as a safe-state sweep, without consulting the current state (src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c:236-244)
  • Validate the registry once at initialisation: every configured channel must exist and every channel must be affiliated to a contactor (src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c:108-122)

Constraints

  • Evaluation period: CONT_CheckFeedback is called from BMS_Trigger on every pass, and BMS_Trigger runs at the end of FTSK_RunUserCodeCyclic10ms, so commanded and sampled states are compared at 10 ms in the pinned configuration (src/app/application/bms/bms.c:918 and src/app/task/config/ftask_cfg.c:258-282).
  • Registry size: BS_NR_OF_CONTACTORS is defined as 2 * BS_NR_OF_STRINGS plus BS_NR_OF_CONTACTORS_OUTSIDE_STRINGS, which is 1 in the pinned configuration, giving 3 entries for a single-string system. Every loop in the module is bounded by this macro and every array indexed by the loop variable is declared with it (src/app/application/config/battery_system_cfg.h:232 and 237).
  • Channel bound: the registry validator asserts spsChannel < SPS_NR_OF_AVAILABLE_SPS_CHANNELS, which is the product of the per-IC contactor channel count and the IC count. The same quantity is the size of the peripheral driver's channel arrays, so the assertion is an index bound as well as a configuration check (src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c:115, src/app/driver/config/sps_cfg.h:102).
  • Channel reservation: SPS_NR_OF_REQUIRED_CONTACTOR_CHANNELS is set to BS_NR_OF_CONTACTORS, so the peripheral driver reserves exactly as many channels as the registry needs. The assertion and the reservation agree by construction at the pinned values, and both derive from the same macro (src/app/driver/config/sps_cfg.h:99).
  • Lookup complexity: every command and every state query is a linear scan over the registry with an early break, so cost is proportional to BS_NR_OF_CONTACTORS. With 3 entries this is immaterial; the design has no index structure and would degrade linearly with string count.
  • Command ordering: currentSet is written before SPS_RequestContactorState is called on both the open and the close path. The registry therefore never claims a commanded state that has not been requested of the peripheral.
  • Feedback freshness: CONT_CheckFeedback samples every contactor on every pass and immediately compares, so the compared feedback is at most one pass old and there is no separate staleness flag.
  • Contactor-type uniqueness is not enforced: both CONT_InitializationCheckOfContactorRegistry and CONT_CheckFeedback carry a TODO to add a check that only one contactor of each type is configured per string, so the first-match break in the lookup is currently guaranteed by the registry contents rather than by a check.
  • Feedback-source fallback: the feedback dispatch tests three of the four CONT_FEEDBACK_TYPE_e values and treats the remaining else as the normally-closed case, so an unrecognised or corrupted feedback kind reads as normally closed rather than being rejected.
  • No latching: a feedback mismatch is re-evaluated from scratch on every pass and the module holds no counter, so a transient mismatch clears on the next agreeing pass.

Failure Response

Failure modeDetectionReaction
Configured switch channel does not existFAS_ASSERT(cont_contactorStates[contactor].spsChannel < SPS_NR_OF_AVAILABLE_SPS_CHANNELS) in the registry validatorThe assertion traps during CONT_Initialize. There is no diagnosis entry and no degraded start; the system does not proceed to operate contactors with an invalid registry.
Configured channel exists but is affiliated to something other than a contactorFAS_ASSERT(SPS_AFF_CONTACTOR == channelAffiliation), which queries the peripheral driver rather than trusting the configurationThe assertion traps. This check is what catches two contactor entries sharing one channel, because the first entry written would leave the channel correctly affiliated but a mis-numbered second entry would not.
Contactor registry holds a type outside plus, minus and prechargeThe default arm of the type switch in CONT_CheckFeedbackFAS_ASSERT(FAS_TRAP) executes and the pass stops. The module treats an unconfigured type as unrecoverable rather than skipping it, which is a deliberate fail-stop on a configuration defect.
Command issued for a string and type the registry does not containThe linear scan completes without a match; the function's own control flow detects itSTD_NOT_OK is returned, no registry field is written and no peripheral request is issued. The failure is silent at the hardware level and does not raise a diagnosis entry.
Contactor does not reach the commanded state, for example welded or mechanically stuckCONT_CheckFeedback compares currentSet against the sampled feedback each pass and finds them unequalThe diagnosis entry for that contactor type is raised with DIAG_EVENT_NOT_OK at DIAG_STRING impact. The module does not retry, does not latch and does not escalate; the reaction belongs to the diagnosis subsystem and the BMS state machine.
A contactor has no feedback source configuredNot a failure: the CONT_HAS_NO_FEEDBACK configuration is handled by substituting the commanded stateThe comparison is satisfied by construction and the diagnosis entry is always cleared. Such a contactor is permanently reported as healthy.
Loss of the 30 V supply to the contactor electronicsThe BMS state machine reaches the substate that handles supply-voltage lossCONT_OpenAllContactors requests every registry channel off, SPS_SwitchOffAllGeneralIoChannels requests the general IO channels off, and the machine leaves through the open-strings-exit substate. This is the one bulk path in the module and it is unconditional, matching the source comment that a request is issued regardless of current state because the intent is to reach a safe state.
Out-of-range string or undefined contactor type reaches a command entry pointFAS_ASSERT on each argumentThe assertion traps before the scan, so the STD_NOT_OK return can never carry this meaning.

Renner' (synthetic scenario character; not a foxBMS maintainer, not SoftwareDevLabs staff, not a real person)", "disposition": "approved", "rationale": "The supplier limit is mandatory, so the change cannot be rejected; there is no design freedom in the ceiling itself. The board therefore dispositions the request as approved in the fictional workflow sense and accepts the availability cost, because the safety margin increase (100 mV -> 150 mV to the FB2-ASM-002 runaway boundary) dominates a false-positive rate that is still bounded by the same 1E-6 events/hour criterion. Three dispositions are bundled and are each independently required: raise the debounce count from 2 to 3 to hold the false-positive rate; rebuild the warning/derating/shutdown ladder so that warning < derating < shutdown below the new ceiling; and reissue FB2-ASM-001 and FB2-ASM-005 rather than editing them in place, because their premises (cell operating range, noise sigma) are what changed."}

Impact analysis{"affected_artifacts": ["FB2-SAF-FSR-000002", "FB2-SAF-HAZ-000001", "FB2-HW-TSR-000001", "FB2-SW-DSN-000002", "FB2-VER-TMS-000001"], "affected_evidence": [], "affected_links": ["FB2-LNK-SAF-000001", "FB2-LNK-SAF-000003", "FB2-LNK-SAF-000009", "FB2-LNK-SAF-000012", "FB2-LNK-SAF-000022", "FB2-LNK-SAF-000023", "FB2-LNK-SAF-000033"], "affected_reviews": [], "risk_assessment": "The change is safety-improving in the hazard sense and availability-degrading in the noise sense, and those two effects pull in opposite directions. (1) Safety margin grows: FB2-ASM-002 places the thermal-runaway boundary above 4300 mV, so tripping at 4150 mV leaves 150 mV of boundary margin where the current 4200 mV limit leaves 100 mV. (2) Availability degrades: FB2-ASM-005 bounds measurement noise at sigma <= 5 mV, and FB2-SAF-FSR-000002 accepts a false-positive rate of 1E-6 events/hour for a 2-consecutive-sample debounce. At a 4200 mV limit the 3-sigma band (4215 mV) lies entirely above the limit, so a single noisy sample rarely crosses it; at 4150 mV the 3-sigma band (4165 mV) sits only 15 mV above the limit, so single-sample excursions below 4150 mV become materially more likely and a 2-of-2 rule starts tripping on noise. (3) The threshold ladder collapses: FB2-PRM-000001 currently carries warning=4150, derating=4180, shutdown=4200, so the new ceiling equals the existing warning level and the three-step ladder must be rebuilt rather than shifted. (4) The measurement-range statement in FB2-HW-TSR-000001 (2.5 V-4.2 V) narrows at the top end, and the plausibility stimulus in FB2-VER-TMS-000003 is specified against that range. (5) Assumptions FB2-ASM-001 and FB2-ASM-005 are invalidated and must be reissued, which in turn invalidates the noise basis of the accepted false-positive criterion. No residual risk is accepted: the debounce count is raised from 2 to 3 to restore the accepted false-positive rate at the new limit."}

Impact analysis{"affected_artifacts": ["FB2-SYS-HSI-000001", "FB2-HW-TSR-000001", "FB2-HW-TSR-000002", "FB2-SW-SWR-000001", "FB2-SW-DSN-000001", "FB2-VER-TMS-000003", "FB2-VER-TMS-000005"], "affected_evidence": [], "affected_links": ["FB2-LNK-SAF-000005", "FB2-LNK-SAF-000006", "FB2-LNK-SAF-000008", "FB2-LNK-SAF-000011", "FB2-LNK-SAF-000027", "FB2-LNK-SAF-000028", "FB2-LNK-SAF-000031"], "affected_reviews": [], "risk_assessment": "This is the highest-exposure change of the three, because the migration removes a safety barrier rather than moving a threshold. (1) The galvanic barrier disappears. FB2-SYS-HSI-000001 specifies iso_spi_transformer_isolation_vrms of 2500, so today the MCU-to-slave monitoring link is a transformer-isolated bus; a direct SPI/DMA link to an ADES1830 sitting at pack potential has no such barrier, and the cell-voltage acquisition path that feeds the ASIL D FB2-SAF-FSR-000001 therefore becomes reachable across a potential difference that the present design deliberately avoids. (2) The communication-integrity requirement becomes about a different failure physics. FB2-HW-TSR-000002 specifies BER < 1E-9, failure detection within 5 ms and 100% CRC coverage for isoSPI; a transformer-isolated differential pair and a direct single-ended SPI bus do not have the same common-mode immunity, and the 5 ms detection time was a property of the isolated link's framing, not of the AFE. (3) The accuracy premise is device-specific. FB2-ASM-005 derives the 5 mV noise sigma from the +/-1.5 mV accuracy that FB2-HW-TSR-000001 states over a 2.5 V-4.2 V range; a different AFE has a different error budget, and that sigma is the entire basis of the false-positive criterion in FB2-SAF-FSR-000002. (4) The driver architecture is device-bound. FB2-SW-DSN-000001 carries the constraint 'SPI clock <= 1 MHz (LTC6811 spec)' and maps four LTC-family translation units; the PEC mechanism, the DMA buffer size of 256 bytes per slave and the state machine are all written against one device family. (5) Timing assumptions with a named premise lapse. FB2-ASM-004 states the < 5 ms SPI-plus-DMA-plus-PEC latency and attributes it to the LTC6811/6813 datasheet at 1 MHz, so the premise of a reissued assumption is required before the latency claim can stand. (6) A new, unanalysed attack surface appears. Replacing an isolated bus with a physically probeable direct bus changes what an attacker can reach; the corpus TARA FB2-SAF-TAR-000001 covers network, serial and diagnostic-write threats and contains nothing that depends on the AFE link's galvanic isolation, so this is recorded as a gap in the threat analysis rather than as a claim that a threat has been assessed. No residual risk is accepted by this record: the isolation loss is dispositioned as deferred-to-a-follow-up rather than as accepted, because a compensating barrier is an architecture decision, not a change-control decision."}

Impact analysis{"affected_artifacts": ["FB2-SAF-FSR-000002", "FB2-SW-DSN-000002", "FB2-SW-SWR-000002", "FB2-VER-TMS-000001"], "affected_evidence": [], "affected_links": ["FB2-LNK-SAF-000009", "FB2-LNK-SAF-000012", "FB2-LNK-SAF-000022", "FB2-LNK-SAF-000023", "FB2-LNK-SAF-000033"], "affected_reviews": [], "risk_assessment": "The safety exposure is availability and trust, not a missing safety function, and the distinction matters for how the fix is reviewed. (1) No hazard is created: the protective reaction still occurs, and it occurs sooner than it should. FB2-SAF-HAZ-000001 lists 'All HV contactors open' and 'Vehicle propulsion disabled' as safe states for the cell-voltage hazard, and a spurious entry into those states is a conservative failure in the safety sense. (2) The exposure is that the ASIL D path becomes untrustworthy. A monitor that reports a fault that is not present trains the operator and the service technician to disregard it, and a de-energised contactor under load at an arbitrary moment is itself a wear event. The realistic field consequence is repeated, unjustified loss of propulsion that a technician cannot reproduce, which is a maintenance-attrition failure mode rather than a hazard. (3) The mechanism is a design-implementation divergence, not a design defect. FB2-SW-DSN-000002 already specifies the transition DEBOUNCING -> IDLE, triggered by 'back_in_limits', guarded by 'voltage within limits', with the action 'reset_debounce'. The design is correct and complete on this point; the implementation does not perform the action the design names. That is why this record does not revise the design, and it is a materially different finding from a missing design element. (4) The requirement permitted the divergence. FB2-SW-SWR-000002 states 'a debounce of 2 consecutive violations within 100 ms' and FB2-SAF-FSR-000002 repeats it, and neither says what happens to a partially advanced counter when the value returns in range. A requirement that specifies the trigger count but not the reset semantics leaves the reset behaviour unspecified, which is how an implementation that never resets can pass a conformance review. (5) Verification did not catch it. FB2-VER-TMS-000001 exercises an excursion, a repetition, and then a single in-range value; it never performs a sequence of excursions each followed by recovery, which is the only sequence in which a missing reset is observable. (6) Interaction with CR-001: raising the debounce count from 2 to 3 as commissioned by FB2-MAN-CHG-000001 makes this defect worse, not better, because the counter is advanced more often and survives more opportunities to be wrongly confirmed. Fixing the reset is a precondition of baselining the new debounce count, not a parallel activity."}

FB2-VER-TMS-000021 — Test: every transferred cell-voltage value is integrity-checked before any decision consumes it, and every published value carries a usable age

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Test typeintegration

Oracle basissource_grounded

Oracle detail{"kind": "source_grounded", "oracle_kind": "source_grounded", "residual_risk": "A source-grounded oracle rests on the code doing what this pass read it to do. If the invalid flag were cleared downstream before a decision reads the block, this oracle would still pass.", "what_it_still_does_not_prove": "It does not prove the corrupted frame is rejected at the AFE rather than merely marked, and it does not prove any downstream decision in the reference project actually consults the invalid flag rather than the raw value. It says nothing about the acquisition rate, which is the fourth acceptance criterion and is covered elsewhere.", "what_the_oracle_is_not": "It is not a measured reference: no block header was read from a running system in this authoring pass, so the property is asserted from the code and not yet observed. It is not an analytical model: no arithmetic model of the integrity path was computed. It is not a synthetic assumption: the property asserted is a property of the code that exists, not an assumption about this programme.", "why_this_oracle": "The oracle is the mechanism the pinned source itself defines, read from the code rather than from the item's output. 'A transferred value whose recomputed packet error code differs from the received one is marked invalid, and an invalid value is not consumed by a decision' is what LTC_CheckPec (ltc_6813-1.c:3838-3878) and the invalidCellVoltage flag it sets at line 641 do. 'A published block carries an age' is what DATA_CopyData (database.c:164-196) does when it copies previousTimestamp and sets timestamp from OS_GetTickCount on every write. Both properties are therefore falsifiable against the source without running the item, which is what makes them usable as oracles at all."}

ObjectiveConfirm two of FB2-SYS-SYR-000001's four acceptance criteria against the pinned source's own mechanism: that the integrity of every transferred value is decided before any decision uses it, and that each published value carries an age that can be read. The integrity criterion is judged against LTC_CheckPec's per-LTC comparison and the fact that a PEC mismatch marks the cell-voltage entry invalid before the parsed values reach the database; the age criterion is judged against the database header timestamp that every write path stamps. The acquisition-rate criterion is deliberately NOT verified here: its figure is a modelled parameter and is covered by a separate measure with a different oracle.

FB2-VER-TMS-000023 — Test: an excursion into each safe-operating-area tier produces the graded reaction the pinned source actually configures, and only the safety-limit tier reaches the fault reaction

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Test typeintegration

Oracle basissource_grounded

Oracle detail{"kind": "source_grounded", "oracle_kind": "source_grounded", "residual_risk": "A source-grounded oracle here is only as good as the read of the configuration table. The table is generated from the configuration headers, and a mismatch between the header and the table would not be caught by reading the table alone.", "what_it_still_does_not_prove": "It does not prove the reference project's degraded mode is reached from the outer tiers. It shows the outer tiers do not open contactors; whether the reference project does anything else with them is a separate question this oracle does not answer. It also says nothing about timing, which is the criterion covered by FB2-VER-TMS-000025.", "what_the_oracle_is_not": "It is not a measured reference: no configuration was read out of a running system. It is not an analytical model: no arithmetic model of the reaction chain was computed. It is not a synthetic assumption: the grading is a property of the configuration table that exists.", "why_this_oracle": "The oracle is the grading the pinned configuration states, read from diag_cfg.c at the pinned commit and from the nested comparison structure of SOA_CheckVoltages. FB2-SYS-SYR-000002 requires the item to distinguish a recoverable degradation from a limit violation, and whether the source can make that distinction at all is a question about the configuration, not about a run: a configuration in which every tier were fatal could not distinguish anything, and the source's is not that."}

ObjectiveEstablish, against the pinned source rather than against the item's output, which of FB2-SYS-SYR-000002's reactions the code can produce. SOA_CheckVoltages compares each string's extremes against three nested tiers per direction - operating, recommended safety and maximum safety - and raises a diagnosis entry per crossed tier; the configuration table then decides what each entry means. Reading the configuration at the pinned commit shows the maximum-safety entries configured as fatal errors with a delay and the two outer tiers configured as a warning and an information entry with the delay discarded, so an excursion into an outer band is recorded and produces no contactor opening. The measure records that grading as the source-grounded part of the requirement.

FB2-VER-TMS-000026 — Test: the limit applied, and the reaction reached, depend on the mode or direction in which the condition occurs

Oracle basissource_grounded

Oracle detail{"kind": "source_grounded", "oracle_kind": "source_grounded", "residual_risk": "Two mechanisms are checked that are not the one the requirement names. The requirement asks for reaction selected by mode; the source selects temperature limits by current direction and initialisation requests by state. It is not a synthetic assumption: the branching is in the source.", "why_this_oracle": "The oracle is the branching the pinned source performs. The temperature path contains an explicit test of the current's sign that selects between two threshold sets, and the request path contains an explicit test of the current state that returns one of several distinct refusal values. Both are properties of code that exists, readable at the pinned commit, and falsifiable by changing one condition in either."}

ObjectiveConfirm that FB2-SYS-SYR-000004's core claim is falsifiable against the pinned source: that the limit applied and the reaction reached are selected by the mode or direction rather than fixed. Two independent mechanisms in the source select on mode or direction. SOA_CheckTemperatures chooses between a discharge tier set and a charge tier set from the sign of the string current, so the same temperature passes or fails depending on direction. The application's state machine selects the contactor reaction from the item's own state and from the requests allowed in that state, and BMS_CheckStateRequest refuses an initialisation request outside the uninitialised state. Both are read from the pinned source and both can be falsified without running the item.

FB2-VER-TMS-000028 — Test: a current or temperature measurement whose trust cannot be established is marked invalid before any supervisory comparison consumes it

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Test typeintegration

Oracle basissource_grounded

Oracle detail{"kind": "source_grounded", "oracle_kind": "source_grounded", "residual_risk": "The gating is per-string and the flag is set per channel, so a partially valid string is represented by a per-string flag whose granularity is coarser than the flag the callback sets. Whether that coarseness can mask a channel-level fault is not examined here.", "what_it_still_does_not_prove": "It does not prove the third criterion. 'Invalid measurements reaching a supervisory decision unchallenged: 0' is a statement about every consumer of the block, and this measure only inspects one consumer, the current-limit comparison. Any other consumer that reads the raw value rather than the flag would pass this measure and violate the requirement. Enumerating those consumers is the missing work and is recorded as such.", "what_the_oracle_is_not": "It is not a measured reference: neither gate was exercised by a run in this authoring pass. It is not an analytical model: no magnitude arithmetic is involved. It is not a synthetic assumption: the gating is in the source.", "why_this_oracle": "The oracle is the gating the pinned source performs, read from two places. The current-sensor receive callback marks every affected channel invalid on a channel error and clears it on reset, at can_cbs_rx_cs_isabellenhuette-ivt-s.c:206-246, and SOA_CheckCurrent reads invalidStringCurrent before it compares anything at soa.c:271-279. Those two facts together are exactly FB2-SYS-SYR-000006's first two criteria, and both are falsifiable by changing one condition in either place."}

ObjectiveConfirm FB2-SYS-SYR-000006's validity-marking and envelope-check criteria against the pinned source. Two independent gates are available. On the acquisition side, the current-sensor receive callback sets the per-string invalidMeasurement flag on every channel error it handles and clears it on reset, so an untrusted measurement is marked at the boundary rather than at the consumer. On the consumption side, SOA_CheckCurrent skips a string's comparison entirely when the database reports that string current invalid, so an invalid value cannot raise a limit diagnosis. The third criterion, that invalid data never reaches a decision unchallenged, is only partly falsifiable from the source, and the measure says which part and which part not.

Oracle basissynthetic_assumption

It is not a requirement test: passing FB2-SAF-FSR-000002 in a unit test says the limit comparison works on synthetic input, which is a different claim from saying a real pack is not cut off.", "why_this_oracle": "The oracle is a stakeholder-intent oracle, not a computed threshold: the judgement is the pack manufacturer's own acceptance criterion that the item shall not take capacity away through false reactions. This corpus has no such agreed criterion, so the acceptance figures below are engineering proposals, and the oracle is therefore synthetic rather than source-grounded or measured."}

ObjectiveConfirm that a pack operated correctly at its published charge limit produces no spurious safe-state reaction over a full charge, because the pack manufacturer's stated need is that the item does not reduce usable capacity through false reactions. This is a false-reaction validation: it does not test that the item detects a real violation (FB2-VER-TMS-000005 does that) but that it stays quiet when it should.

It is not a requirement test: FB2-VER-TMS-000006 and FB2-VER-EXE-000006 exercise the state machine's reaction, which says the state changes and not that a human understands what changed.", "why_this_oracle": "Two oracles are combined and both are declared. The safety half is a source-grounded oracle: the 100 ms figure comes from the safety goal's own FTTI and is checkable by arithmetic against the timing budget. The experience half is a synthetic-assumption oracle: 'actionable to a driver' has no agreed definition in this corpus, and the proposal that it is decided by asking the driver class is a process invention, not a derived criterion."}

ObjectiveConfirm that when a genuine overvoltage reaction occurs while the vehicle is being driven, the outcome is the one the end-user driver stakeholder needs: the pack is isolated, the vehicle coasts to a stop under its own control, and the driver is told what happened in terms that do not require a diagnostic engineer to interpret. This measure exists because the master prompt warns that disconnecting a battery can itself affect propulsion: the safety reaction that satisfies the safety goal may still fail the stakeholder if the driver is left without an explanation.

FB2-VER-TMS-000014 — Validation: degraded operation remains usable and is announced before it becomes a hard stop (operational scenario: single-channel measurement degradation)

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Test typevalidation

Oracle basisanalytical_model

Oracle detail{"oracle_kind": "analytical_model", "what_the_oracle_is_not": "It is not a source-grounded oracle: nothing in the pinned source demonstrates a degraded mode of this shape, and the observed foxBMS diagnosis severities do not map onto the concept's modes one to one. It is not a measured reference: no channel was degraded. It is not a stakeholder oracle: the service class's ability to diagnose the degradation is proposed, not agreed.", "why_this_oracle": "The oracle is derived from the concept's own degraded-operation strategy, not from a measurement of the item. The functional safety concept defines three degraded modes with named retained and removed capability; the acceptance figures check that the item reaches the mode it is specified to reach and escalates at the specified point. The model is the specification's internal consistency, checked against the specification."}

ObjectiveConfirm that a measurement-path degradation moves the item into its degraded mode with a capability the pack manufacturer can still use, and that the reduction is announced before the condition becomes a hard stop. The failure this guards against is specific: a degraded mode that silently removes capability, or one that escalates to a full safe state on the first degradation, makes the item unusable in service without ever being unsafe, which is a different and equally real defect.

FB2-VER-TMS-000015 — Validation: the service technician can commission and service the item without being able to energise it incorrectly (operational scenario OS-006, workshop service)

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Test typevalidation

Oracle basissynthetic_assumption

Oracle detail{"oracle_kind": "synthetic_assumption", "what_the_oracle_is_not": "It is not a source-grounded oracle: the observed source contains a commissioning mode and a maintenance pin behaviour, but the procedure written here is authored, not extracted, and the real foxBMS documentation does not contain this procedure. It is not an analytical model: nothing computes executability. It is not a measured reference: no technician has performed it.", "why_this_oracle": "The oracle is the documented procedure itself: a step is conformant when it can be performed in the stated order and the item's response matches what the step says. The 'a technician completes it without improvising' criterion is a process oracle that this corpus cannot settle, because the technician is a declared fictional stakeholder and no usability study exists."}

ObjectiveConfirm that a service technician following the documented commissioning and service procedure cannot bring the item into a state in which the contactors are commanded closed with open-circuit sensor inputs, and that the procedure's steps are executable in the order given. The stakeholder need is the service class's: a procedure that is technically correct but not executable in sequence causes technicians to improvise, and improvisation is how commissioning errors reach a vehicle.

It is not a synthetic assumption in the sense of an assumed behaviour: the assumption is about a configuration value, and it is recorded as a parameter rather than asserted as a fact about code.", "why_this_oracle": "The oracle is the arithmetic of the requirement itself. FB2-SYS-SYR-000001 asks for at least 20 acquisitions per second; the reference project records a 50 ms acquisition period; 1000/50 is 20. No item needs to run for the comparison to have a verdict, and the verdict is sensitive to exactly one input, which is what makes recording that input the substantive part of the measure."}

ObjectiveCompute whether the reference project's configured measurement period meets the acquisition-rate criterion of FB2-SYS-SYR-000001, and record the arithmetic rather than an observation. The criterion is at least 20 acquisitions per second in every monitoring mode; the parameter registry records the acquisition period as 50 ms (FB2-PRM-000003); 1/0.050 s is 20 per second exactly, so the criterion is met with zero margin at the configured value and fails for any period longer than 50 ms. The measure exists because the criterion's figure is a modelled parameter and not a figure any code or measurement in this corpus establishes, which is a different kind of claim from the integrity criterion and needs a different oracle.

ObjectiveCompute whether the reaction chain the pinned source implements can close inside the interval FB2-SYS-SYR-000003 allocates, and record the arithmetic. The oracle is the sum of the configured waits the source actually applies between the stages of opening, taken from the application configuration at the pinned commit, compared against the allocated interval and against the contactor-mechanical figure the parameter registry records. The measure is expected to fail, and recording that it fails - with the arithmetic shown - is the honest result rather than a defect in the measure.

FB2-VER-TMS-000024 — Test: the debounce and the degraded-to-fault boundary FB2-SYS-SYR-000002 demands, against an explicitly labelled synthetic assumption

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Test typeunit

Oracle basissynthetic_assumption

Oracle detail{"kind": "synthetic_assumption", "oracle_kind": "synthetic_assumption", "residual_risk": "An assumption-labelled oracle can only ever confirm that the requirement is internally consistent with the assumed behaviour. It cannot detect that the assumption is the wrong shape of behaviour, which is the failure mode that matters most here.", "what_it_still_does_not_prove": "It does not prove the reference project can implement the debounce without introducing a new failure mode, and it does not prove the diagnosis layer's occurrence counter cannot be configured to behave equivalently - which, if it could, would make the requirement satisfiable without new code and would make the proposed counter in FB2-SW-IMP-000002 unnecessary. That question is open and is recorded as open.", "what_the_oracle_is_not": "It is not source_grounded: the pinned source contains no debounce, so nothing about the classification outcome can be read off it. It is not an analytical model: no model of the counter's timing was computed. It is not a measured reference: nothing was measured.", "why_this_oracle": "The oracle is an assumption this record states outright: that the reference project, once built, would count consecutive violations per cell and classify only on the second one inside a 100 ms window. The expected outcomes follow from that stated assumption and from nothing else. No measurement, no model and no source property is being appealed to, which is precisely why the record names this kind rather than borrowing a stronger-sounding one."}

ObjectiveVerify the two parts of FB2-SYS-SYR-000002 that have no counterpart in the pinned source and can therefore only be judged against a stated assumption: that a classification requires two consecutive violations within 100 ms, and that a numerical or named rule separates the degraded reaction from the fault reaction. The oracle is declared a synthetic assumption and the assumption is stated in the record rather than hidden in a fixture: the debounce the reference project specifies is the debounce it would have to build, and the boundary value would have to be declared before it could be tested. The measure's value is that it makes the absence concrete - the source implements no SOA debounce at all, and the diagnosis layer's occurrence counter is a different mechanism with different parameters, so the requirement's debounce criterion is not merely untested here, it is unimplemented in the code the reference project would reuse.

FB2-VER-EXE-000001 — Execution: SOA Voltage Limit Test (real macOS host run)

profile as_is · origin source_observed · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false
