FB2-VER-TMS-000028 — Test: a current or temperature measurement whose trust cannot be established is marked invalid before any supervisory comparison consumes it

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Test typeintegration

Oracle basissource_grounded

Oracle detail{"kind": "source_grounded", "oracle_kind": "source_grounded", "residual_risk": "The gating is per-string and the flag is set per channel, so a partially valid string is represented by a per-string flag whose granularity is coarser than the flag the callback sets. Whether that coarseness can mask a channel-level fault is not examined here.", "what_it_still_does_not_prove": "It does not prove the third criterion. 'Invalid measurements reaching a supervisory decision unchallenged: 0' is a statement about every consumer of the block, and this measure only inspects one consumer, the current-limit comparison. Any other consumer that reads the raw value rather than the flag would pass this measure and violate the requirement. Enumerating those consumers is the missing work and is recorded as such.", "what_the_oracle_is_not": "It is not a measured reference: neither gate was exercised by a run in this authoring pass. It is not an analytical model: no magnitude arithmetic is involved. It is not a synthetic assumption: the gating is in the source.", "why_this_oracle": "The oracle is the gating the pinned source performs, read from two places. The current-sensor receive callback marks every affected channel invalid on a channel error and clears it on reset, at can_cbs_rx_cs_isabellenhuette-ivt-s.c:206-246, and SOA_CheckCurrent reads invalidStringCurrent before it compares anything at soa.c:271-279. Those two facts together are exactly FB2-SYS-SYR-000006's first two criteria, and both are falsifiable by changing one condition in either place."}

ObjectiveConfirm FB2-SYS-SYR-000006's validity-marking and envelope-check criteria against the pinned source. Two independent gates are available. On the acquisition side, the current-sensor receive callback sets the per-string invalidMeasurement flag on every channel error it handles and clears it on reset, so an untrusted measurement is marked at the boundary rather than at the consumer. On the consumption side, SOA_CheckCurrent skips a string's comparison entirely when the database reports that string current invalid, so an invalid value cannot raise a limit diagnosis. The third criterion, that invalid data never reaches a decision unchallenged, is only partly falsifiable from the source, and the measure says which part and which part not.

FB2-VER-TMS-000016 — Verification: an unauthenticated peer is refused service, and an authenticated session's payload is neither readable nor alterable by a passive or active segment observer

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Test typerobustness

Oracle basissource_grounded

Oracle detail{"kind": "source_grounded", "oracle_kind": "source_grounded", "residual_risk": "A source-grounded oracle still rests on the implementation using the mechanism the requirement names. If the implementation used a different mechanism, this oracle would be measuring the wrong thing.", "what_it_still_does_not_prove": "It does not prove the item uses such a mode, that the key is stored well, that the mode is non-negotiable, or that the authentication cannot be bypassed by a different path. It also cannot prove the 'confidentiality of session data' acceptance criterion as a field observation, only as an inspection against the protocol's own guarantees.", "what_the_oracle_is_not": "It is not a measured reference: no capture exists and nothing was replayed. It is not an analytical model: no model of the key exchange is computed here. It is not a synthetic assumption: the property asserted is a property of a primitive, not an assumption about this programme.", "why_this_oracle": "The oracle is the cryptography's own definition, read from the requirement rather than from the implementation. 'A peer that cannot produce the key cannot produce a session it can decrypt' is a property of authenticated encryption, and it is checkable against the implementation by inspection: if the item uses an authenticated mode with a key the peer must possess, an observer without the key recovers nothing, and a modified frame fails authentication by definition of the mode. The expected outcomes are therefore not copied from what the item produced; they are what the chosen mode permits."}

ObjectiveConfirm that the master software completes no externally reachable network session with a peer that has not authenticated, and that after authentication the session's application payload is neither recoverable in plaintext by an observer on the segment nor modifiable by one. Also confirm that each refusal is diagnosable, because a silent refusal cannot be distinguished from an outage during field analysis.

FB2-VER-TMS-000017 — Verification: a peer holding the maximum permitted connections open and silent does not deny service to legitimate peers

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Test typerobustness

Oracle basisanalytical_model

Oracle detail{"kind": "analytical_model", "model_sensitivity": "Availability under exhaustion falls as C rises. At C = 4 with a 2000 ms timeout the worst case is that 4 of the pool are blocked for at most 2 s each. Raising C to 16 without shortening T would make a silent peer able to consume four times the blocked-time budget, which is why the requirement fixes both figures rather than one.", "oracle_kind": "analytical_model", "what_it_still_does_not_prove": "The model says nothing about a peer that stays within the caps and still consumes the service's CPU through a cheap request pattern, nor about a peer that opens and closes rapidly enough to churn through the cap. It also cannot prove the 'resources released' part of the breach criterion, which is a code-path property no external model reaches.", "what_the_oracle_is_not": "It is not a measurement: no service was starved and nothing was timed. It is not a source-grounded oracle: the caps are engineering choices, not properties of a protocol, and the requirement carries them as proposals. It is not a synthetic assumption about the world, though it is an assumption about the implementation: the model holds only if the implementation actually enforces the caps rather than declaring them.", "why_this_oracle": "The oracle is a resource model rather than an observation. A service with a hard cap C on concurrent connections and a finite receive timeout T cannot be starved by a peer that sends nothing: at most C connections can be blocked for at most T each, after which their resources are reclaimed, so the steady-state availability of the remaining capacity is a function of C and T and not of how long the hostile peer holds its sockets. The expected outcomes are the model's outputs - C, T, the byte budget and the breach-response time - each chosen so the model closes: 4 connections at a 2000 ms timeout bounds the blocked-time budget, and a 128 KiB burst exceeds the 65536-byte budget by a factor of two so the breach is unambiguous."}

ObjectiveConfirm that a hostile peer cannot make the service unavailable to a legitimate peer by opening the maximum number of permitted connections and sending nothing on them, and that every refusal and every budget breach is diagnosable. This is the measure for the requirement's availability clause; the resource figures it checks are the requirement's own, not figures this measure chooses.

FB2-VER-TMS-000018 — Verification: a bus peer without the shared secret cannot present a frame the dispatch layer accepts

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Test typerobustness

Oracle basissource_grounded

Oracle detail{"kind": "source_grounded", "known_limitation_in_the_requirement": "The requirement's genuine-frame false-rejection criterion was revised under finding FB2-REV-FND-000028. It used to be an absolute '0 frames over 24 h', which no implementation that genuinely verifies integrity can meet - a keyed integrity value of width w rejects a genuine frame with probability 2^-w, so over a long campaign the expected count is non-zero for any practical w - and which an implementation that rejected every frame would satisfy vacuously. The criterion now bounds the rate at 1 per 10^6 genuine frames, demonstrated as 0 rejections over a genuine-frame population of at least 3 x 10^6, and requires the integrity value to be at least 22 bits. What that does NOT bound: it bounds the rate at the population stated and nowhere else, so a campaign that observes fewer than 3 x 10^6 genuine frames cannot demonstrate it and this measure must record the population it actually observed. It also says nothing about the behaviour of the receiver under an authenticated peer that is entitled to send a frame it is not entitled to send, nothing about resynchronisation after a desynchronising error, and nothing about the secrecy of the key. A key that is short, hard-coded or recoverable from the firmware image satisfies every expected outcome here and still gives no authenticity.", "oracle_kind": "source_grounded", "what_it_still_does_not_prove": "The oracle proves the dispatch layer's verdict, not the secrecy of the key. A key that is short, hard-coded, or recoverable from the firmware image satisfies every expected outcome here and still gives no authenticity. The revised false-rejection bound additionally does not prove the integrity value is well chosen, only that it is at least 22 bits wide and that the observed false-rejection rate over the observed population is consistent with 1 per 10^6. It does not prove the counter's initial value is unpredictable, which is the property FB2-SAF-SEC-000005 addresses and which this measure must not be read as covering.", "what_the_oracle_is_not": "It is not a measured reference: no bus was instrumented and nothing was injected. It is not a synthetic assumption: the properties asserted are properties of counter discipline and keyed integrity, both of which hold or fail independently of this item. It is not an analytical model of the bus: bus load, arbitration and error frames are outside it.", "why_this_oracle": "The oracle is the arithmetic of the check itself, taken from the requirement and independent of the item. A counter establishes freshness only if the receiver's expected value is not derivable from observed traffic, which is exactly the property a strict-increment counter with a seeded initial value has and a zero-based counter does not. A frame-integrity value a peer cannot produce without the shared secret establishes authenticity because the receiver recomputes it over the payload and compares; a modified payload necessarily fails the comparison, and a forged one necessarily fails unless the peer holds the key. A data-length check is a direct comparison. Each expected outcome - zero accepted - is a consequence of the check existing, not a number read out of a run."}

ObjectiveConfirm that for every CAN identifier whose payload influences a safety function, a frame carrying a valid identifier but no valid counter, no valid integrity value or the wrong data-length code is rejected before the receive callback is invoked, and that a genuine frame with a sequence error is rejected rather than accepted out of order.

FB2-VER-TMS-000019 — Verification: the serial link acts only on authenticated frames, and the XOFF/XON byte values are demoted to ordinary payload

profile synthetic_reference · origin synthetic · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Test typerobustness

Oracle basissource_grounded

Oracle detail{"kind": "source_grounded", "known_limitation_in_the_requirement": "As with the CAN measure, the 'genuine frames rejected: 0' criterion was unsatisfiable for a practical integrity value and has been revised under finding FB2-REV-FND-000028. It now bounds the rate at 1 per 10^6 genuine frames, demonstrated as 0 rejections over a genuine-frame population of at least 3 x 10^6, and requires the integrity value to be at least 22 bits. The bounds it does not carry are the same as the CAN measure's: the bound holds only at the population stated, and it says nothing about the secrecy of the key, about resynchronisation after a desynchronising error, or about whether an authenticated peer is entitled to command what it commands.", "oracle_kind": "source_grounded", "what_it_still_does_not_prove": "The oracle says nothing about the strength of the integrity value, about re-synchronisation after a desynchronising error, or about whether an authenticated peer is entitled to command what it commands. It also does not cover the availability consequence: a receiver that discards everything malformed but never resynchronises passes every expected outcome here and is unusable.", "what_the_oracle_is_not": "It is not a measured reference: no serial traffic was sent or captured. It is not an analytical model: there is no model of the receiver's parser. It is not a synthetic assumption: admissibility is decidable by the receiver by construction.", "why_this_oracle": "The oracle is the framing rule's own definition, read from the requirement. A frame is admissible only when its declared length equals the received byte count and its integrity value verifies; both are decidable by the receiver alone, so a byte outside such a frame has no admissible interpretation and must be discarded. The control-byte clause follows from the same definition: 0x13 and 0x11 are payload byte values, and a value that is privileged only inside an authenticated frame cannot be reached outside one. The expected outcomes - zero bytes passing, zero transitions - are consequences of the rule, not observations of an implementation."}

ObjectiveConfirm that no byte on the serial receive line reaches the application layer without passing a length check and an integrity check, that a structurally valid frame with a modified payload is rejected, that neither 0x13 nor 0x11 can change the transmit-enabled state outside an authenticated frame, and that a receive overflow is diagnosable.

It does not prove that any component is free of known vulnerabilities; a complete, evidenced, freshly checked inventory containing a vulnerable component passes every expected outcome here. It does not prove the advisory source is authoritative or that its coverage is adequate.", "what_the_oracle_is_not": "It is not a source-grounded oracle: nothing in the pinned source demonstrates a sound entropy source, and the requirement's own rationale records the opposite. It is not a measured reference: no sequence number was collected and no advisory was queried. It is not an analytical model: no entropy estimate is computed. It is a synthetic assumption, and the assumption it makes is that distinctness plus a non-fixed seed is worth recording while the real property remains unmeasured.", "why_this_measure_is_still_worth_running": "A requirement whose verification plan contains no oracle at all will never be verified however long it is planned. Recording the weakest oracle that can honestly be applied, together with an explicit statement of what it cannot see, is the step that makes the gap visible. The honest next step is not this measure but an advisory-source review performed by an authorised party, which is outside this corpus entirely.", "why_this_oracle": "Neither clause has an oracle available to it, and saying so is the honest answer rather than borrowing one. Unpredictability is not observable from outside: the measure checks distinctness, which is a necessary condition for unpredictability and far from sufficient, and it checks that the seed is not fixed at build time, which the observed source's own annotation says is currently not the case. A generator that is entirely predictable and never repeats would pass this measure. The inventory clause is worse: 'checked against an authoritative advisory source' has no oracle at all, because this corpus consulted no advisory source and has no authority to consult one, so the expected outcomes here are checks on the RECORD of checking, and the record is the thing under test."}

ObjectiveTwo clauses with two different oracles, stated separately rather than blended. First: confirm that the initial TCP sequence number takes a distinct value on every one of 1000 connection establishments and that the entropy seed is distinct across 1000 power cycles. Second: confirm that every entry in the component inventory carries either evidenced version information or an explicit null with a stated reason, that no entry carries a guessed version, that the inventory has been checked against an authoritative advisory source within the stated interval, and that every match has a recorded adjudication including the determinations that found nothing.

Referenced requirementsFB2-SAF-SEC-000005

Referenced designsFB2-SYS-SYR-000007, FB2-SYS-SYR-000008

Preconditions
  • The item's network stack is reachable and the source can be inspected for the seed's origin.
  • A power-cycle fixture exists that records the seed at each boot.
  • The component inventory exists as a maintained document with an owner.
  • An authoritative advisory source exists and the project is permitted to consult it. This last precondition is NOT satisfied in this corpus, which is why this measure cannot produce a pass even in principle.

Anomalies
AnomalyDescription
macOS is not a supported foxBMS 2 host platform. cli/cmd_embedded_ut/embedded_ut_impl.py resolves the Ceedling project file with get_platform(), which returns only 'linux' or 'win32' and raises SystemExit at import time for any other value (embedded_ut_impl.py:88-91). The upstream entry point 'fox.py ceedling' therefore cannot be used on macOS at all. This run reproduced that entry point's build layout manually in an isolated workspace under docs/artifacts/.work/verification-env/ without modifying cli/.
HALCoGen, the proprietary Texas Instruments code generator, is not available on this host. The repository ships its inputs (conf/hcg/app.hcg, conf/hcg/app.dil) but not its output; conf/hcg/include/ and conf/hcg/source/ are gitignored and empty. Per tools/waf-tools/f_hcg.py:150-157 the only artefact the host build needs from HALCoGen is include/config_cpu_clock_hz.h, which was regenerated with HALCOGEN_CPU_CLOCK_HZ=100000000 read out of the repository's own conf/hcg/app.dil (DRIVER.OS.VAR.OS_CPUCLOCKHZ.VALUE). A minimal stand-in for HL_spi.h, which tests/unit/support/struct_helper.h includes for the single type spi_config_reg_t, was reconstructed from the public TMS570 SPI configuration register map. It is NOT the TI original and provides no register offsets, functions, enums or macros.
Apple clang rejects the three TI section-placement attributes defined in src/os/freertos/freertos/include/mpu_wrappers.h (PRIVILEGED_FUNCTION, PRIVILEGED_DATA, FREERTOS_SYSTEM_CALL all use section(".kernelTEXT") and similar), because Mach-O requires a 'SEGMENT,SECTION' pair. GNU/Linux ELF accepts them, so this is a macOS-only build failure. A force-included shim (foxbms_host_port_shim.h) pre-defines the mpu_wrappers.h include guard so those three macros become empty. The attributes only control target image layout and have no effect on test semantics.
The compiler driver named by the shipped configuration is 'gcc'. On macOS /usr/bin/gcc is the Apple clang driver, so the test binaries are Mach-O rather than ELF. Diagnostics that Apple clang enables by default but GNU gcc does not under the same -std=c11 -Wextra -Wall -pedantic -Werror set were suppressed (-Wno-strict-prototypes, -Wno-deprecated-non-prototype). Each suppresses a diagnostic only.
Ceedling 1.1.9 aborts on this test tree with :use_test_preprocessor: :all, failing in the preprocessor's directive-only pass with "Failed to read './test/preprocess/files/<test>/directives_only/raw/ftask.h' for comment stripping ... No such file or directory". The value was set to :none, which selects Ceedling's own documented source-scan fallback and resolves the same headers. This is a Ceedling-side workaround in the isolated copy of the project file only.
The project file :use_backtrace: :gdb requires an executable named 'gdb' on PATH or Ceedling refuses to start. GNU gdb does not ship with macOS. A shim at bin/gdb forwards the backtrace request to LLDB. It runs only when a test binary crashes and never influences a pass/fail verdict.
The Ceedling project file was reproduced byte-identically from the shipped conf/unit/app_project_posix.yml and then rewritten only in the isolated copy. The four rewrites are: :use_test_preprocessor :all to :none, a force-include of foxbms_host_port_shim.h, and the two -Wno- diagnostic flags. No file under src/, tests/, conf/, tools/, cli/, gui/, hardware/ or the repository-root wscript, fox.py or fox.sh was modified.
The test file named by the previous record, tests/unit/app/driver/ltc/6813-1/test_ltc_6813-1.c, does not exist in this checkout; the 'afe/' path segment is missing. The real file is tests/unit/app/driver/afe/ltc/6813-1/test_ltc_6813-1.c. evidence_refs has been corrected.
SIL supersession. tests/unit/app/driver/afe/ltc/6813-1/test_ltc_6813-1.c now BUILDS and RUNS under the SIL harness and its assertions pass, because sil/iface supplies host-declared HL_can.h, HL_het.h, HL_reg_can.h, HL_reg_het.h and HL_reg_system.h and the module under test can_cfg.c/can.c compile against them. What that establishes is the driver's logic and the structure of the arguments it hands to the TI HAL. It establishes NOTHING about the CAN/HET register map, which remains unobtained. This record therefore stays execution_kind=none / outcome=blocked; the host-run evidence is recorded separately and is not presented as closing the requirement.

This supersedes the blocked state recorded in FB2-VER-EXE-000004. That record's `unblocking_conditions` required a real HALCoGen run, because 'this test exercises the LTC SPI/HET transfer path and would not be meaningful against a stubbed register map'. The SIL harness meets that requirement only in part: it verifies the driver's logic and the argument structure it hands to the HAL, and it does NOT verify the register map. The register map remains unobtained and the unverified claim is stated explicitly rather than implied.
The blocked set is 200, not the 177 the earlier closure reported. See FB2-VER-EXE-000015 anomaly 2. 23 tests were undercounted because the closure walked only the test file's own include closure and not the module under test Ceedling links in; 19 of those 23 are hidden behind upstream's :paths: exclusion of the ades183x and mc3377x AFE directories.

FB2-SW-DEV-000001 — Deviation: Directive-4.1 loop-counter / accumulation casts in MRC_ValidateBatteryVoltageMeasurement (redundancy.c) - one record, 3 suppressed sites

profile as_is · origin source_observed · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

GuidelineMisraC2012

Rule referenceDirective-4.1

Rule categoryadvisory_directive

Suppression formdisable_enable_block

Suppression scopeblock

Deviation typedeliberate_truncation_of_wider_value

Deviation rationaleValues start with 0, iteration is less than UINT8_MAX; overflow impossible

Reanalysis justificationThe two block suppressions are justified by a bound argument ('iteration is less than UINT8_MAX') that depends on BS_NR_OF_STRINGS staying below UINT8_MAX and on stringVoltage_mV staying inside int32_t. Neither bound is checked at run time and neither is stated in the record. The third site (line 680, AXIVION Next Codeline Style MisraC2012Directive-4.1) is a different claim: 'we sum INT32 values x times and divide by x, resulting in INT32'. The top-level affected_lines and suppression_form therefore cover only the two Disable/Enable block sites, 658-662 and 669-673; the Next Codeline site at 680-681 is carried in the deviations[] entry below, because a record's top-level suppression_form is single-valued and cannot represent both annotation forms. All three must be re-analysed if the string count, the cell-voltage type or the redundancy summation width changes, and the truncation of a 64-bit accumulator to int32_t at line 682 should be re-checked against the worst-case pack voltage.

Normative verification{"conformance_claimed": false, "rule_severity_asserted": false, "rule_text_reproduced": false, "status": "rule_reference_unverified_against_proprietary_source"}

Review dispositionrecorded_inline_no_governance_evidence

Review disposition noteGovernance evidence search at the pinned baseline: no deviance log, deviation log, suppression register, waiver file or review record for the MisraC2012 style checks exists anywhere in the repository (searched for *deviance*, *deviation*, *misra*, *axivion* file names and for 'AXIVION' across docs/). docs/tools/static-analysis/ and conf/spa/ do not exist at this commit. The rationale text below is therefore the only recorded justification.

Impact notes[{"aspect": "type_safety", "note": "sumOfStringValues_mV is declared int64_t and accumulated in a loop bounded by BS_NR_OF_STRINGS, but the result is truncated to int32_t by the cast at line 682; the suppression itself covers the loop counters, not that final cast."}, {"aspect": "runtime_behavior", "note": "When no string is closed (numberOfConnectedStrings == 0) the function averages over all valid strings, and when none is valid it publishes batteryVoltage_mV = INT32_MAX with invalidBatteryVoltage = 1. The suppressed loop is on both branches."}, {"aspect": "safety_argument", "note": "This is the redundancy cross-check path. FB2-SW-DEV-000002 — Deviation: MisraC2012-1.2 shared-RAM section placement of the ADI ADES183x PEC buffers (adi_ades183x.c)

profile as_is · origin source_observed · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

GuidelineMisraC2012

Rule reference1.2

Rule categoryrule

Suppression formdisable_enable_block

Suppression scopeblock

Deviation typememory_section_placement

Deviation rationaleThe Pec buffer must be put in the shared RAM section for performance reasons

Reanalysis justificationThe section placement is a toolchain-dependent, linker-script-dependent construct. Re-analyse on any change to the linker command file, the .sharedRAM output-section definition, the DMA cache configuration for the AFE channels, or the buffer size ADI_N_BYTES_FOR_DATA_TRANSMISSION, because the shared section is a scarce, non-cacheable RAM region and moving or growing these buffers can silently collide with other DMA consumers.

It must be re-analysed on every HALCoGen re-generation, on any mailbox renumbering, and on any change of the TI Hercules CAN driver register map, because a stale block silently reverts mailbox configuration while still reporting no violation. The recorded provenance (HL_can.c, 11-Dec-2018, version 04.07.01) should be pinned in a configuration-managed baseline rather than in a source comment.

Only MisraC2012-2.2 is in the MISRA rule set, so this record carries that rule and lists the other three as co-located non-MISRA checks. No approval or waiver artifact for the vendored block was found in the repository. Governance evidence search at the pinned baseline: no deviance log, deviation log, suppression register, waiver file or review record for the MisraC2012 style checks exists anywhere in the repository (searched for *deviance*, *deviation*, *misra*, *axivion* file names and for 'AXIVION' across docs/). docs/tools/static-analysis/ and conf/spa/ do not exist at this commit. The rationale text below is therefore the only recorded justification.

Deviation rationaleRegister ISR

Reanalysis justificationThe rationale 'Register ISR' is the shortest in the set and states no constraint that could be checked. FB2-SW-DEV-000013 — Deviation: MisraC2012-1.1 integer-to-pointer casts in I2C_WriteReadDma, two suppressed sites in one symbol

profile as_is · origin source_observed · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

GuidelineMisraC2012

Rule reference1.1

Rule categoryrule

Suppression formdisable_enable_block

Suppression scopeblock

Deviation typetype_conversion_for_hardware_register_access

Deviation rationaleCast necessary for DMA configuration

Reanalysis justificationTwo suppressions in one function because it configures a transmit and then a receive DMA channel. Re-analyse the pair together: the transmit buffer and the receive buffer must both satisfy the same placement and width assumptions, and a change to one without the other would leave the function half-suppressed. Re-trigger on buffer type/size change, on DMA channel remapping, and on any change to the I2C interrupt-driven state machine around the two OS_EnterTaskCritical / OS_ExitTaskCritical windows.

FB2-SW-DEV-000014 — Deviation: MisraC2012-21.10 dependency on the hosted <time.h> implementation in rtc.c

profile as_is · origin source_observed · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

GuidelineMisraC2012

Rule reference21.10

Rule categoryrule

Suppression formdisable_enable_block

Suppression scopeblock

Deviation typestandard_library_dependency

Deviation rationaleTime implementation is suitable for the application

Reanalysis justificationThe rationale 'Time implementation is suitable for the application' is an assertion, not an argument: no property of the <time.h> implementation is named, and the claim depends entirely on which C library the TI ARM CGT runtime supplies. It is also asserted for a 584-line region (lines 70-653) that is 580 times larger than the '#include <time.h>' at line 71 that it appears to justify, so any 21.10 finding anywhere in the module is silenced by a statement written about the include alone. It must be re-analysed on any change of compiler, runtime library, or time source, and on any addition of code to rtc.c outside the include; the specific time functions actually used from <time.h> should be enumerated in the justification. The 21.10 suppression region also encloses the separate MisraC2012-1.2 Disable/Enable pair at lines 77 and 84, which is recorded on its own as FB2-SW-DEV-000015; the 'Time implementation is suitable for the application' rationale therefore does not cover the DMA-buffer section-placement code at rtc.c:77-84, and that nested site must be re-analysed under its own record.

FB2-SW-DEV-000016 — Deviation: MisraC2012-2.2 redundant shift expressions in the seven SPI hardware chip-select masks (spi_cfg-helper.h)

profile as_is · origin source_observed · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

Rule reference2.2

Rule categoryrule

Suppression formdisable_enable_block

Suppression scopeblock

Deviation typereadability_vs_redundancy

Deviation rationaleRedundant expressions are kept to enhance code readability

Reanalysis justificationSeven separate, identical Disable/Enable pairs, one per chip-select mask, at 79/89, 93/103, 107/117, 121/131, 135/145, 149/159 and 163/173; each pair is also wrapped in clang-format off/on. The masks must be re-analysed whenever a chip-select bit position constant changes, whenever a new CS line is added, and whenever the surrounding clang-format region is moved, because the suppression is scoped to source-line adjacency. A consolidation of the seven masks into a single block-level suppression would be a legitimate simplification but would also hide any new 2.2 finding in the same header.

Impact notes[{"aspect": "runtime_behavior", "note": "Each mask ORs six shifted literals into the CSNR field: five carry SPI_HARDWARE_CHIP_SELECT_NOT_ACTIVE (1) and exactly one carries SPI_HARDWARE_CHIP_SELECT_ACTIVE (0). Spelling out all six positions, including the zero-valued one, is what makes the de-selected line explicit. A wrong term changes which AFE slave is selected, i.e. which cell voltages are read."}, {"aspect": "maintainability", "note": "The rationale is a readability trade-off, which is the weakest justification class in this set: the same result can be obtained by a table-driven or single-mask formulation that static analysis accepts."}, {"aspect": "verification_coverage", "note": "The masks are exercised only through the AFE driver path; no as_is unit-test artifact in the corpus targets spi_cfg-helper.h directly."}]

FB2-SW-DEV-000019 — Deviation: MisraC2012-10.4 for the FAS_STATIC_ASSERT block asserting the predefined bool / STD_RETURN_TYPE_e values (application general.h)

profile as_is · origin source_observed · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

GuidelineMisraC2012

Rule reference10.4

Rule categoryrule

Suppression formdisable_enable_block

Suppression scopeblock

Deviation typestatic_assert_on_predefined_macro_values

Deviation rationaleThese assertions have to check the actual values of the enums and defines.

Reanalysis justificationThe suppressed check flags comparison of a value with an unnamed literal, which is exactly what these six assertions do by design. Re-analyse if fstd_types.h changes the representation of bool or STD_RETURN_TYPE_e, if a unit-test configuration redefines them, or if new invariant assertions are added to the block, since the Disable/Enable pair is a single block. The assertion is a compile-time gate, so a change in these values breaks the build rather than runtime behaviour, which lowers but does not remove the re-analysis need.

FB2-SW-DEV-000021 — Deviation: Directive-4.9 and MisraC2012-20.7 for the function-like GEN_STRIP parenthesis-stripping macro (application general.h)

profile as_is · origin source_observed · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

GuidelineMisraC2012

Rule referenceDirective-4.9

Rule categoryadvisory_directive

Suppression formdisable_enable_block

Suppression scopeblock

Deviation typepreprocessor_macro_required_by_language_subset

Deviation rationaleFunction-like macro needed for this feature. Parenthesis stripping is intended here.

Reanalysis justificationGEN_STRIP(x) expands to GEN_GET_ARGS x, which is a deliberate parenthesisation trick: it only works because a parenthesised argument is accepted as a single macro argument and then unwrapped. It therefore silently succeeds or fails based on how the caller wrote the argument, which no static analysis can fully check. Re-analyse on every new GEN_STRIP call site, on any change to the GEN_REPEAT_U family that consumes it, and whenever the tool's CertC-PRE01 support changes, since the Disable/Enable mismatch on that family leaves the intended extent undetermined.

Normative verification{"conformance_claimed": false, "rule_severity_asserted": false, "rule_text_reproduced": false, "status": "rule_reference_unverified_against_proprietary_source"}

The suppression extent is therefore ambiguous: under the literal reading CertC-PRE01 remains enabled and the rationale claims to cover it. No waiver artifact was found. FB2-SW-DEV-000023 — Deviation: Directive-4.1 for the 64-bit CRC signature split into the two 32-bit CRC peripheral registers (bootloader crc.c)

Rule referenceDirective-4.1

Rule categoryadvisory_directive

Suppression formdisable_enable_block

Suppression scopeblock

Deviation typedeliberate_truncation_of_wider_value

Deviation rationalethis cast is supposed to only extract one part (32 high bits) of 64-bit CRC signature stored in the root variable.

Reanalysis justificationOne block-level Disable/Enable pair covers two separate casts with two separate rationales, so the suppression extent is a superset of both claims. Re-analyse if the CRC hardware register width changes, if the CRC polynomial or signature width changes, or if CRC_NUM_OF_BITS_PSA_SIGREGH1 is retuned; the shift amount is the load-bearing constant and nothing in the record states its value or its derivation. The same file carries a third Directive-4.1 suppression at line 312, but it is not on this record's symbol: line 312 sits inside crcNotification, a different function from CRC_SemiAutoCrcCalculation, so it is outside both this record's query scope and the symbol this record names. It is therefore referenced here in prose only and is deliberately not enumerated in deviations[], because listing a line range from another function under this record's affected_symbol would misstate the span. Its rule exposure belongs to the crcNotification symbol.

FB2-SW-DEV-000026 — Deviation: MisraC2012-10.4 for the bootloader FAS_STATIC_ASSERT block asserting the predefined bool / STD_RETURN_TYPE_e values

profile as_is · origin source_observed · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

GuidelineMisraC2012

Rule reference10.4

Rule categoryrule

Suppression formdisable_enable_block

Suppression scopeblock

Deviation typestatic_assert_on_predefined_macro_values

Deviation rationaleThese assertions have to check the actual values of the enums and defines.

Reanalysis justificationSame re-analysis triggers as the application copy: a change to the representation of bool or STD_RETURN_TYPE_e, a unit-test configuration that redefines them, or a new invariant added to the block. Because the block is duplicated per build target, both copies must be re-analysed when fstd_types.h changes.

Normative verification{"conformance_claimed": false, "rule_severity_asserted": false, "rule_text_reproduced": false, "status": "rule_reference_unverified_against_proprietary_source"}

Review dispositionrecorded_inline_no_governance_evidence

Review disposition noteThe identical assertion block and identical suppression exist in the application copy of general.h (FB2-SW-DEV-000019), so the invariant is duplicated per build target. Governance evidence search at the pinned baseline: no deviance log, deviation log, suppression register, waiver file or review record for the MisraC2012 style checks exists anywhere in the repository (searched for *deviance*, *deviation*, *misra*, *axivion* file names and for 'AXIVION' across docs/). docs/tools/static-analysis/ and conf/spa/ do not exist at this commit. The rationale text below is therefore the only recorded justification.

FB2-LNK-SEC-000015synthetic_referenceFB2-SAF-TAR-000001supportsFB2-SAF-FSR-000003Threat THR-007 is a hypothetical-project threat against a planned diagnostic and configuration write service, not a threat observed in the pinned source. FB2-LNK-CHG-000001synthetic_referenceFB2-MAN-CHG-000001changesFB2-SAF-FSR-000002The ASIL D limit-monitoring requirement names the debounce count and the false-positive criterion. CR-001 moves both, so the requirement is a declared target of the change request.syntheticpendingtruerev 1 → rev 2
FB2-LNK-CHG-000002synthetic_referenceFB2-MAN-CHG-000001changesFB2-SAF-HAZ-000001The hazard record expresses its degraded state in terms of the derating level, and this change rebuilds the warning/derating/shutdown ladder that defines it. FB2-LNK-CHG-000003synthetic_referenceFB2-MAN-CHG-000001changesFB2-HW-TSR-000001The AFE accuracy requirement is stated over a 2.5 V-4.2 V measurement range. FB2-LNK-CHG-000004synthetic_referenceFB2-MAN-CHG-000001changesFB2-SW-DSN-000002The SOA detailed design carries the constraint 'Debounce count configurable (default: 2)'. FB2-LNK-CHG-000005synthetic_referenceFB2-MAN-CHG-000001changesFB2-VER-TMS-000001The limit-monitor test embeds the ceiling in its stimulus text ('above 4200 mV limit') and the debounce count in its step count. FB2-LNK-CHG-000006synthetic_referenceFB2-MAN-CHG-000002changesFB2-SYS-HSI-000001The interface authority carries iso_spi_transformer_isolation_vrms = 2500 in its electrical budget. FB2-LNK-CHG-000007synthetic_referenceFB2-MAN-CHG-000002changesFB2-HW-TSR-000001The AFE accuracy requirement states a device-specific error budget (+/-1.5 mV over 2.5 V-4.2 V). FB2-LNK-CHG-000008synthetic_referenceFB2-MAN-CHG-000002changesFB2-HW-TSR-000002All three acceptance criteria of this requirement - BER < 1E-9, failure detection within 5 ms, CRC coverage 100% - describe an isolated differential link. FB2-LNK-CHG-000009synthetic_referenceFB2-MAN-CHG-000002changesFB2-SW-SWR-000001The AFE driver software requirement is written against one device family's validation mechanism and DMA shape. FB2-LNK-CHG-000010synthetic_referenceFB2-MAN-CHG-000002changesFB2-SW-DSN-000001The driver architecture is bound to one device in an explicit part-number constraint, in a DMA buffer size that follows from that device's frame, and in an implementation mapping whose every row is an LTC path.syntheticpendingfalserev 1 → rev 1
FB2-LNK-CHG-000011synthetic_referenceFB2-MAN-CHG-000002changesFB2-VER-TMS-000003The plausibility stimulus bounds are the direct product of the front end's error budget and full-scale range. FB2-LNK-CHG-000012synthetic_referenceFB2-MAN-CHG-000002changesFB2-VER-TMS-000005The only test exercising communication integrity injects faults into the isolated link's framing. FB2-LNK-CHG-000013synthetic_referenceFB2-MAN-CHG-000003changesFB2-SAF-FSR-000002The ASIL D requirement specifies how many consecutive violations confirm a fault but says nothing about a partially advanced counter when the value returns in range. FB2-LNK-CHG-000014synthetic_referenceFB2-MAN-CHG-000003changesFB2-SW-DSN-000002The SOA design already specifies the DEBOUNCING -> IDLE transition with the action reset_debounce, so the design is correct and is not revised. FB2-LNK-HW-000001synthetic_referenceFB2-HW-HVP-000001depends_onFB2-HW-HCB-000001The hardware verification plan is scoped by the configuration baseline: the plan's own scope_basis names FB2-HW-HCB-000001 and takes the board set and the released versions from it rather than choosing them. Without that dependency the plan's subject would be undefined, since the release index is the only place in this repository that says which boards exist and at which versions. The direction is plan to baseline: the plan is the finer statement and the baseline is what it rests on.derivedpendingfalserev 1 → rev 1
FB2-LNK-HW-000002synthetic_referenceFB2-HW-HDD-000001depends_onFB2-HW-HCB-000001The HWE.3 gap record repeats the same search result that the configuration baseline records: zero Altium source files in the working tree and in every commit, and the designs hosted on an external server. The gap record does not re-derive that from scratch, it depends on the baseline's measurement and extends it with the count of the records that inherit the limitation. If the baseline's availability finding were wrong, this record would be wrong too, so the dependency is declared rather than left implicit.derivedpendingtruerev 2 → rev 1
FB2-LNK-HW-000003synthetic_referenceFB2-SYS-HVA-000001refinesFB2-HW-HCB-000001The system-domain variant applicability record refines the hardware configuration baseline at the system level. The baseline fixes seven board designations and ten released versions; the applicability record states which of them a system requirement can be stated against, and records the three board designations the variant registry names for which the release index releases nothing. It is the finer statement: it answers a question the baseline does not ask.derivedpendingfalserev 1 → rev 1
FB2-LNK-IFS-000004synthetic_referenceFB2-SW-IFS-000001refinesFB2-SW-DSN-000001The AFE design record's interfaces field is a signal table: it names cell_voltages as uint16_t[] in mV at 20 Hz and says nothing about who calls it, what the legal string range is or how a failure is reported. FB2-SW-IFS-000001 replaces that table with the six declared elements of the API, their real signatures, the assertion that bounds the string argument, the two-value return contract and the 1 ms period the calling task imposes. It refines FB2-SW-DSN-000001, the architecture record whose signal table it supersedes, and is at the same level as FB2-SW-DSN-000004, the detailed design record for the same element: it adds the interface contract that the detailed design record also does not carry.derivedpendingfalserev 1 → rev 1
FB2-LNK-IFS-000005synthetic_referenceFB2-SW-IFS-000002refinesFB2-SW-DSN-000002The SOA design record's interfaces field is a signal table naming fault_request as bool and violation_details as a struct at event rate. FB2-SW-IFS-000002 replaces it with the four declared elements of the module, three of which return void and register diagnosis events, and the fourth of which is declared and called on the 10 ms cycle and does nothing. It refines FB2-SW-DSN-000002 and sits alongside FB2-SW-DSN-000005, which designs the debounce internally and still carries no interface contract.derivedpendingfalserev 1 → rev 1
FB2-LNK-IFS-000006synthetic_referenceFB2-SW-IFS-000003refinesFB2-SW-DSN-000003The contactor design record's interfaces field is a signal table naming the command and feedback signals. FB2-LNK-IFS-000007synthetic_referenceFB2-SW-IFS-000004refinesFB2-SW-IMP-000004The CAN implementation record maps the transport to named symbols in the pinned source. FB2-LNK-SIR-000020synthetic_referenceFB2-SW-SIR-000001specified_byFB2-SW-IFS-000001FB2-SW-SIR-000001 is the software interface requirement set for the acquisition and monitoring boundary and is specified by FB2-SW-IFS-000001 (AFE measurement driver API) and FB2-SW-IFS-000002 (SOA supervision). The direction is specification to requirement, which is the direction a requirement is written in: the interface specification establishes what the interface is by analysing the source at the pinned commit, and the requirement states what must be true of it. This is the opposite of the direction the three existing FB2-SW-SWR-* requirements were produced in - those are back-inferred from the implementation and their revision history says so - and naming the relationship explicitly is what keeps the two directions distinguishable. Every statement in the requirement is traceable to a named element of the specification, and the requirement carries that traceability as a field rather than leaving it in prose.derivedpendingfalserev 1 → rev 1

FB2-REV-000018 — Review: the sixteen software interface specifications, their source fidelity at the pinned commit and the honesty of their interface-level gap lists

profile synthetic_reference · origin derived · human_approval_status pending · production_authorized false · product_verification_credit false

review typedomain

scopeFull scope over all sixteen software_interface_specification records in the corpus: FB2-SW-IFS-000001 through FB2-SW-IFS-000016, every one at revision 1. All sixteen declare profile 'synthetic_reference' and there is no as_is software_interface_specification record in this corpus, so this single profile-scoped review covers every record of the type and no reviewed_id below resolves ambiguously. FB2-REV-FND-000046 records why that matters: a profile-scoped review cannot cover both profiles' records under a shared identifier, because doing so would assert that one review examined two different records that share a string. It is checked here rather than assumed - see review_method.per_profile_check. Each record's full text was read, and every source citation it makes was checked by reading the blob at commit 308028fb rather than the working tree, because the records' own method is 'source_analysis_at_pinned_commit' and verifying that claim against the working tree would not verify it. NOT IN SCOPE: whether the sixteen interfaces are correctly specified, whether the described behaviour is the behaviour the product should have, whether the consuming modules named exist with the responsibilities attributed to them, and the assembler routine behind FAS_DisableInterrupts, which is outside the C language boundary these records declare.

No human reviewer signed any of them.; No artifact covered by this review carries production authority or product verification credit. All sixteen declare production_authorized false and product_verification_credit false, and this review asserts neither.; WHAT WAS ACTUALLY VERIFIED, and how: (a) every declared source_refs entry was resolved against docs/artifacts/sources/source-registry.json - 81 of 81 resolve, 0 dangling; (b) for every element of every record, the declared symbol was searched for on the declared declaration_line and implementation_line in the blob at commit 308028fb, read with git show so that the working tree was never consulted - 61 of 61 declaration lines carry the claimed symbol, 60 of 61 implementation lines do; (c) every 'path Lnn' and 'path Lnn-Lmm' citation appearing anywhere in the sixteen records was resolved in the blob at the same commit and range-checked against the file's real length - 572 of 572 in bounds, 0 outside, 0 unparseable, 0 naming a file absent from the commit; (d) the same check applied to interface_level_gaps evidence alone: 70 of 70 in bounds; (e) the anti-conformance fields were read field by field on all sixteen; (f) a pattern search for conformity, certification, capability-level, qualified-checker and organizational-independence language was run over the serialized text of all sixteen and every hit was read in context - 0 unnegated claims; (g) every standards_mappings entry was read for status - 0 of 30 entries claim 'mapped', all are 'partially_mapped'; (h) the oracle and execution fields were read on all sixteen.; WHAT WAS NOT VERIFIED, and this is the larger half: whether any of the sixteen interfaces is correctly specified. A source citation can be exact and the specification built on it can still be wrong - a misread control flow, a wrong caller, a mis-stated consequence. This review checked that the records point at the source accurately; it did not check that their reading of the source is right. No C file was analysed for behaviour beyond confirming that a named symbol occurs on a named line, so a claim of the form 'the timer guard returns at L286' was checked for line existence and not for whether line 286 is the timer guard.; No C file was compiled, linked or executed. No test was run against any of these interfaces. Nothing here is evidence that any interface behaves as described at run time, and the records themselves say so: all sixteen declare verification_status with analysed_against_running_code false and conformance_tested false, and not one of the sixteen claims verification of any kind.; The consuming modules named by the sixteen records were NOT checked to exist, and no interface agreement was checked for. A consuming module named in consumption_evidence was accepted as named. This is a real gap in the review's coverage and is stated rather than left implicit.; The assembler routine behind FAS_DisableInterrupts was located for the purposes of FB2-REV-FND-000195 and its dispatch was read, but its body was NOT analysed and no claim is made about what it does. The sixteen records place it outside their declared boundary and this review does not cross that boundary.; The sixteen records' own interface_level_gaps were checked for structure and for citation resolvability only. Whether each gap is the RIGHT gap - whether a more consequential interface-level problem was missed - is a completeness judgement that this review does not make and does not claim.; The single wrong line reference found (FB2-REV-FND-000193) was found by exhaustive automated checking of all 61 implementation lines and all 572 prose ranges. The check is sound for the class 'does this line exist, is it in bounds, does it carry this symbol'. It cannot detect a citation that is in bounds and carries the right symbol but attributes the wrong significance to it. A residue of semantically-wrong-but-positionally-correct citations is therefore not excluded, and quantifying it would require reading each of the sixteen against its source in full, which is a re-authoring exercise rather than a review.; The 16 parameters carrying neither valid_range nor range_evidence were examined and are NOT a finding. Each is the placeholder entry for a zero-parameter function, named '(none)', emitted so that the parameters array is never empty; there is no parameter for a range to describe. Recorded here so that a reader who runs the same mechanical check does not report it as a defect.

root causeThe rule tests only the SOURCE side of a verifies/validates relation, while the corpus's link convention places the test measure at the source and the requirement at the target. Under that convention the rule cannot be satisfied by any requirement that is verified in the corpus's own idiom, so it fires on every safety requirement that has a test. The rule is not wrong to exist - it is the MUT mutation detector for a missing verification link - but its firing on a well-verified requirement is a direction mismatch between the rule and the registry convention, not a traceability defect.

root causeThe rule tests only the SOURCE side of a verifies/validates relation, while the corpus's link convention places the test measure at the source and the requirement at the target. Under that convention the rule cannot be satisfied by any requirement that is verified in the corpus's own idiom, so it fires on every safety requirement that has a test. The rule is not wrong to exist - it is the MUT mutation detector for a missing verification link - but its firing on a well-verified requirement is a direction mismatch between the rule and the registry convention, not a traceability defect.

impactThis is a real and open verification gap, not a rule artefact. Five security requirements - authenticated transport, bounded connection admission, CAN message integrity and freshness, serial-link framing and authorisation, and strong entropy plus component governance - carry the entire cybersecurity concept and none of them is verified by anything in the corpus. The security case in this corpus therefore rests on requirements that have no verification evidence at all, and the acceptance criteria that would make them verifiable were written but never turned into a measure.

The security case in this corpus therefore rests on requirements that have no verification evidence at all, and the acceptance criteria that would make them verifiable were written but never turned into a measure.

evidenceThree figures in the corpus disagree about the same reaction. FB2-SAF-FSR-000003 states: acceptance criterion 'Contactor open latency, Time from FAULT request to contactor feedback open, 30 ms'; rationale '30 ms mechanical opening + 5 ms feedback = 35 ms within FTTI budget'; and the safety goal's timing_budget.allocation gives contactor_command 5 + contactor_mechanical 30 + feedback_verification 5 = 40 ms after the fault request. The requirement's own threshold is therefore 10 ms tighter than its own arithmetic and 5 ms tighter than the budget it is spending from. FB2-SAF-FSR-000003 also state…

impactA requirement whose threshold is tighter than its own mechanism's budget will fail, and when it fails the failure will look like a defect in the contactor driver rather than a defect in the requirement, so the engineering effort goes to the wrong place. It also makes the safety goal's 100 ms interval unverifiable at the end of the chain: the existing acceptance criteria, taken together, claim a reaction that is faster than the sum of the recorded parts. Any verification measure written against FB2-SAF-FSR-000003 inherits an unachievable threshold.

evidenceFB2-SAF-FSR-000004's rationale reads: 'addresses timing budget violation in main path (115 ms > 100 ms FTTI) by providing parallel safety channel'. FB2-HW-TSR-000004 repeats the same sentence word for word. No record in the corpus contains 115 ms. The nearest figure is FB2-SAF-SGO-000001's allocation, whose serial elements sum to 85 ms for the main path. 115 is neither 85 (the actual sum) nor 105 (the sum plus the recorded margin), so it cannot be reconstructed from the corpus at all.

impactThe justification for adding an independent ASIL B hardware channel - a substantial hardware cost and the basis of the ASIL D decomposition - rests on a number that cannot be located or reproduced. A reader checking the arithmetic finds nothing to check, and the most likely reading is that the figure was estimated at some point and never reconciled. The independent monitor may well be justified; the justification as written does not support it.

12. Declared Gaps

Every place where the engineering process expects content the corpus does not hold is listed here as a named gap. The registry is built from the same calls the section renderers make, so it cannot drift from the body: a gap is registered at the moment the renderer discovers the absence, and the mandated wording not specified in corpus is what the body shows at that site. Nothing below is filled with a plausible substitute, and nothing is omitted silently.

13. Diagram Validation

13. Diagram Validation

No diagram in this document is described as validated by this file. The diagrams are emitted as Mermaid source and rendered by the reader's browser from a CDN. The syntax check is a separate post-generation step, run by the operator, whose result is reported on the console and deliberately not embedded here — embedding it would make the file depend on the outcome of an external tool and would break the byte-for-byte determinism the integrity check enforces. The table below therefore records, for every diagram, its identifier, its Mermaid diagram type, its viewpoint and the exact corpus fields it is derived from. It makes no syntax claim.

StepCommand or fact

plan idFB2-MAN-MSM-000001

separation from product evidenceEvery metric in this plan measures the development process. None of them measures the product's behaviour, and none of them carries product verification credit. A metric that reaches 100 percent says the project's records are complete and honest; it says nothing about whether the battery management system is safe. The corpus-wide product evidence dimension is computed separately and is zero for target hardware, and the two numbers must never be added together or quoted in the same sentence without this sentence.

aspice process idSUP.8

definitionConfiguration management is the identification, baselining, change control and status accounting of the corpus's records. Every record carries a profile, a baseline id, a revision and a revision history, and every link carries the revisions of both endpoints. A change to a baselined item goes through the change-control process and not through this one; this process identifies and baselines, that one decides.

Regeneration and Integrity

What the integrity check verifiesHow
The file exists and is non-emptystat and size
Every required section anchor and heading is presenteach sec-* id and heading string from the generator's section registry
Every required sub-heading is present inside its sectioneach heading from the generator's sub-heading map, searched within that section's text
Every record in the artifact index is anchored in the documenteach (profile, id) in the index must have an art-<profile>-<id> anchor; a missing one is named in the failure output
Every requirement record appearseach cov-<profile>-<id> coverage-matrix row must exist for every requirement record in the index
Every link registry entry appearseach lnk-<profile>-<link id> row must exist for every link
Every gap is registered and every absent-model site carries the mandated wordingthe number of rendered gap registry rows must equal the number of gaps the renderers registered, and the number of gap-phrase spans in the file must equal the number of absent-model sites the renderers passed
Every guard line matches the corpuseach guard element's data-guard attribute is compared against the record's own four guard fields, and its visible text is checked to contain all four
The run is deterministicthe document is generated a second time into a temporary directory and byte-compared after normalising the single data-generated-at attribute
